notes.title: How the cuisine filters were policed
notes.body: Every food card names a specific dish — a label alone doesn’t qualify. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it serves. Tabelog and Retty scores may measure popularity but never count as a source.

notes.title: Web-searched in Japanese and English, fact-checked
notes.body: Every place is traceable to two credible sources, or a lone UNESCO / Agency for Cultural Affairs designation — recorded in data/sources.json. Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked open. Yelp/TripAdvisor/Tabelog never count toward the two-source bar.

places.n: Shuri Castle (首里城)
places.w: Palace of the Ryūkyū Kingdom from 1429 to 1879 and the centrepiece of the UNESCO Gusuku Sites. Destroyed in 1945 and again by fire in 2019; the rebuilt Seiden (main hall) exterior is complete, its interior due to reopen on 23 November 2026.
places.k: UNESCO World Heritage gusuku; Seiden rebuild

places.n: Tamaudun Royal Mausoleum (玉陵)
places.w: Limestone tomb of the second Shō dynasty, built in 1501 under King Shō Shin and modelled on Shuri Castle, its balustrades carved with dragons, phoenixes and lions. A National Treasure as well as a UNESCO component.

places.n: Sonohyan-utaki Ishimon (園比屋武御嶽石門)
places.ad: Shuri Castle Park, Shuri, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: Stone gate to the sacred grove behind it, where Ryūkyū kings prayed for safe journeys before leaving Shuri; a UNESCO component standing beside Shuri Castle Park.

places.n: Shikinaen Royal Garden (識名園)
places.w: The Ryūkyū royal family’s largest villa garden, built around a pond with jagged coral-limestone bridges two kilometres south of Shuri Castle; used to receive Chinese envoys and now a UNESCO component.

places.n: Naminoue Shrine (波上宮)
places.w: Okinawa’s ichinomiya (chief shrine), perched on a coral bluff above Naminoue Beach; long the place where fishermen and sailors prayed for a safe voyage.

places.n: Makishi Public Market (第一牧志公設市場)
places.w: Naha’s kitchen since 1950: 75 ground-floor stalls of spiny lobster, reef fish, pork and island produce, with upstairs restaurants that cook what you buy (mochiage). Reopened in a new building on 19 March 2023.

places.n: Sefa-utaki (斎場御嶽)
places.w: The holiest site of Ryūkyūan religion: a sacred grove of limestone clefts overlooking Kudaka Island, where the kingdom’s high priestess was invested. A UNESCO Gusuku component.

places.n: Nakagusuku Castle (中城城跡)
places.w: Best-preserved of the Ryūkyū castle ruins: six enclosures of curved limestone walls on a ridge above both coasts. UNESCO Gusuku component.

places.n: Nakijin Castle Ruins (今帰仁城跡)
places.w: Hilltop stronghold of the Hokuzan kingdom with long serpentine limestone walls. UNESCO Gusuku component.

places.n: Zakimi Castle Ruins (座喜味城跡)
places.w: Early-15th-century gusuku on a Yomitan hilltop, one of the five castle sites inscribed by UNESCO.

places.n: Katsuren Castle Ruins (勝連城跡)
places.w: Terraced gusuku ruins on the Katsuren peninsula, one of the five castle sites inscribed by UNESCO.

places.n: Bios Hill (ビオスの丘)
places.w: A nature theme park in Uruma's Ishikawa hills: water-buffalo cart rides, lake boat rides through subtropical forest and orchid viewing; you can also try on Ryukyu-era costume. Stars and Stripes Okinawa has covered it repeatedly as a family day out.

places.n: National Theatre Okinawa (国立劇場おきなわ)
places.w: Opened 18 January 2004 as Japan's fifth national theatre, built to preserve and present Okinawan traditional performing arts — above all kumiodori, the Ryukyuan court music-drama. A 632-seat main hall and a 255-seat small hall.

places.n: Agena Castle Ruins (安慶名城跡)
places.w: A gusuku built around 1453 by a local lord (aji) of Agena and a nationally designated Historic Site. Its concentric double ring of stone walls is described by Uruma City as the only surviving example of the type in Okinawa.

places.n: Nakabaru Ruins, Ikei Island (仲原遺跡)
places.ad: Ikei, Uruma, Okinawa (centre of Ikei Island)
places.w: A late-Jōmon-period village site near the middle of Ikei Island and a nationally designated Historic Site, with reconstructed pit dwellings. One of Uruma's four national historic sites.

places.n: Shirumichu sacred cave, Hamahiga Island (シルミチュー霊場)
places.w: A limestone cave up a 108-step stair behind a torii on Hamahiga Island, held to be where the Ryūkyū creator deities Shinerikyo and Amamikyo lived and raised their children — a place of prayer for fertility and harvest. The cave itself is normally closed and opened for Lunar New Year rites.
places.k: Cave home of the creator gods

places.n: Urasoe Art Museum (浦添市美術館)
places.w: Opened in 1990 as Japan's first museum devoted to lacquer art and Okinawa's first public art museum. Its collection centres on Ryukyu lacquerware from the 16th century to today, with 80–100 pieces on show in themed displays that change three times a year; the building is by architect Uchii Shōzō.

places.n: Ryukyu Glass Village, Itoman (琉球ガラス村)
places.w: Okinawa's largest handmade-glass factory, with galleries and shops of colourful Ryukyu glass and first-come glass-blowing classes at its Workshop Think Think. Rurubu lists it as a southern-Okinawa craft stop and Stripes Okinawa has covered its hands-on workshop.

places.n: Minna Island — 'Croissant Island', Motobu (水納島)
places.w: A small crescent-shaped coral island (0.47 km², highest point 26.9 m) off the Motobu Peninsula, nicknamed 'Croissant Island' because it looks like one from the air. The OCVB lists it and its Minna Beach as a day-trip swimming and snorkelling spot.
places.k: The croissant-shaped coral island off Motobu

places.n: Kin Kannon-ji Temple, Kin (金武観音寺)
places.w: A Kōyasan Shingon temple (mountain name Kinpusan, main image Shō-Kannon) traditionally founded in the 16th century by the monk Nisshū, who was shipwrecked at Kin while sailing from Kii and preached from the limestone cave beside the temple. Kin town's tourism site lists the cave (Nisshū-dō) and the temple's old fukugi trees.
places.k: 16th-century temple over the Kin limestone cave

places.n: Fukuji Dam & Lake Fukujō, Higashi (福地ダム・福上湖)
places.ad: Fukuji River, Higashi-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: Completed in 1974 on the Fukuji River, Okinawa's largest dam holds the prefecture's biggest reservoir, Lake Fukujō, chosen in 2005 as one of Japan's 100 best dam lakes. The Yanbaru three-villages tourism portal lists its lookouts, lakeside paths and water-resources exhibit hall, with nature-watching boat and canoe trips on the lake.
places.k: Okinawa's largest dam lake in the Yanbaru forest

places.n: Tōrin-ji & Gongen-dō, Ishigaki (桃林寺・権現堂)
places.w: Gongen-dō, beside Tōrin-ji temple in central Ishigaki, was first built in 1614, destroyed by the great Meiwa tsunami of 1771 and rebuilt; it was designated a national Important Cultural Property in 1981. The Agency for Cultural Affairs' database notes decorative details unusual in mainland shrine architecture and calls it Japan's southernmost surviving early-modern religious building of this scale.
places.k: Japan's southernmost Important Cultural Property shrine hall, rebuilt after the 1771 tsunami

places.n: Okinawa Peace Memorial Park & Prefectural Peace Memorial Museum (平和祈念公園)
places.w: The main memorial to the Battle of Okinawa, on Mabuni Hill where the fighting ended in June 1945. The museum traces the lead-up, the battle and the rebuilding; outside, the Cornerstone of Peace lists every fallen soldier and civilian of every nationality.

places.n: Himeyuri Peace Museum (ひめゆり平和祈念資料館)
places.w: Museum beside the Himeyuri Monument, telling the story of the schoolgirls drafted as nurses into army cave hospitals in 1945, most of whom died. Opened 23 June 1989.
places.nat: ひめゆり平和祈念資料館

places.n: Former Japanese Navy Underground Headquarters (旧海軍司令部壕)
places.ad: Tomigusuku, Okinawa, Japan (Navy HQ park, south of Naha)
places.w: Several hundred metres of hand-dug tunnels and rooms that served as the Imperial Navy's command post in 1945; the walls still bear the shrapnel marks of the officers' last stand.

places.n: Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium (沖縄美ら海水族館)
places.ad: Ocean Expo Park, Motobu, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: Widely rated Japan's best aquarium, at the tip of the Motobu Peninsula. Its Kuroshio Tank — one of the largest in the world — holds whale sharks and manta rays.

places.n: Cape Manzamo (万座毛)
places.w: Grassy clifftop above the Onna coast with the elephant-trunk rock arch; one of the island's most-visited viewpoints.

places.n: Tokei Beach & Heart Rock, Kouri Island (ティーヌ浜)
places.w: The north-shore cove of 'Love Island' Kouri, reached by the long Kouri Ōhashi bridge, where the heart-shaped rock formation stands in the shallows.

places.n: Furuzamami Beach, Zamami Island (古座間味ビーチ)
places.w: Zamami's best beach, a 20-minute walk from the port: 'Kerama blue' water and reef straight off the sand; holds two Michelin Green Guide stars per the village.

places.n: Sunset Beach, Chatan (サンセットビーチ)
places.w: Artificial-bay beach beside Mihama American Village on the west coast, about 250 m of sand facing the sunset.

places.n: Zanpa Beach, Yomitan (残波ビーチ)
places.w: West-coast swimming beach beside Cape Zanpa, reached by airport limousine bus to the cape resort.

places.n: Okinawa World & Gyokusendo Cave (おきなわワールド 玉泉洞)
places.w: Culture park built over Gyokusendo, a 5 km limestone cave (850 m open) — the longest in the south and second-longest in Japan — with a craft village of old houses and a habu snake museum.
places.nat: おきなわワールド 玉泉洞

places.n: Yomitan Yachimun no Sato Pottery Village (やちむんの里)
places.w: Lane of red-tile workshops and climbing kilns founded after Living National Treasure Jiro Kinjo moved his studio here in 1972; around 45–50 potters, with shops selling cups, plates and shisa.

places.n: Cape Zanpa & Lighthouse (残波岬)
places.w: The main island's westernmost cape: 30 m cliffs and Okinawa's tallest lighthouse (31 m), a classic sunset spot, with a park and giant shisa statue.

places.n: Ōjima Island (奥武島)
places.w: Tiny bridge-linked fishing island off Nanjō, famous for cheap fresh-fish and seaweed tempura stands and its many cats.

places.n: Yonaha Maehama Beach (与那覇前浜)
places.w: Seven kilometres of white sand on Miyako's south-west tip, facing Kurima Island — the beach that usually tops rankings of Japan's best.

places.n: Kabira Bay (川平湾)
places.w: Turquoise-to-emerald bay on Ishigaki's north coast, a national Place of Scenic Beauty inside Iriomote-Ishigaki National Park; swimming is banned, so see it by glass-bottom boat over the black-pearl farms.

places.n: Tatami-ishi, Kume Island (畳石)
places.ad: Ōjima, Kumejima, Shimajiri District, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: About a thousand pentagonal and hexagonal andesite columns, each 1–1.5 m across, exposed at low tide on the south shore of Ōjima, bridged to Kume Island — a Miocene lava field that looks like tatami mats.

places.n: Hiji Falls (比地大滝)
places.ad: Kunigami Forest Park, Hiji, Kunigami, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: The main island's tallest waterfall (25.7 m), reached by a forest trail and suspension bridge through the Yanbaru subtropical woods from the Kunigami campground.

places.n: ASMUI Spiritual Hikes (former Daisekirinzan, 大石林山)
places.w: Trails through jagged limestone karst near Cape Hedo, a place of prayer for some 600 years — renamed ASMUI Spiritual Hikes.

places.n: Cape Hedo (辺戸岬)
places.w: The northernmost point of Okinawa Island: jagged limestone cliffs where the East China Sea meets the Pacific, with Yoron Island on the horizon and the Yanbaru-kuina observatory on the hill behind.

places.n: Tsuboya Yachimun-dōri pottery street (壺屋やちむん通り)
places.w: The Ryūkyū Kingdom's ceramics quarter: a 400 m stone-paved street between Kokusai-dōri and Route 330 lined with potteries, kilns and shops selling yachimun ware and shisa, with wheel-throwing classes.

places.n: Mihama American Village (美浜アメリカンビレッジ)
places.w: Reclaimed-land entertainment district with a Ferris wheel, Depot Island's colourful facades, US-style diners and boutiques — the clearest expression of Chatan's base-town melting pot.
places.nat: 美浜アメリカンビレッジ

places.n: Koza Gate 2 Street (コザ ゲート通り)
places.w: The street running to Kadena Air Base's Gate 2, Okinawa's live-music strip since the 1960s–70s: rock, blues and Latin bars alongside Okinawan folk; home of the November International Carnival.

places.n: Kaichū-dōro sea causeway (海中道路)
places.w: Five-kilometre road laid across turquoise shallows from the Katsuren Peninsula to Henza, then bridged on to Hamahiga, Miyagi and Ikei — the island-hop drive of central Okinawa.

places.n: Amamichu, Hamahiga Island (アマミチュー)
places.w: Rocky islet off 'God's Island' Hamahiga, revered as the tomb of Amamikiyo and Shinerikiyo, the creator deities of the Ryūkyū myths; reached on foot across a short causeway.

places.n: Ikei Beach, Ikei Island (伊計ビーチ)
places.w: Reef-sheltered beach on the farthest of the Kaichū-dōro islands, with some of the clearest water reachable by car from the main island.

places.n: Mount Omoto (於茂登岳)
places.w: At 525.5 m the highest peak in Okinawa Prefecture, rising from the Omoto range on Ishigaki's north; a forest trail climbs to views over Kabira and the reef. Paired with Kabira Bay as a national Place of Scenic Beauty.

places.n: Taketomi Island & village (竹富島)
places.w: Fifteen minutes by ferry from Ishigaki: a preserved Ryūkyū village of coral-stone walls, red-tiled houses and white-sand lanes travelled by water-buffalo cart — a national Important Preservation District since 1987 — ringed by Kondoi Beach.

places.n: Kurima Island & Kurima Ōhashi (来間島)
places.w: Small island reached by the 1.7 km Kurima Ōhashi from Miyako's south-west, with café stops and Nagamahama beach looking back across to Maehama.

places.n: Ikema Island & Ikema Ōhashi (池間島)
places.w: Fishing island off Miyako's northern tip, reached by the 1.4 km Ikema Ōhashi over shallow turquoise reef.

places.n: Tōri-ike, Shimoji Island (通り池)
places.w: Two collapsed-cave sinkholes in the coral of Shimoji's west coast — 75 m and 55 m across, linked to each other and the sea by an underwater cave — the 'dragon's eyes', a national Natural Monument and a celebrated cave dive.

places.n: Miyara Dunchi (宮良殿内)
places.w: Residence of a Ryūkyū-kingdom official built in 1819 in the style of Shuri samurai houses — an Important Cultural Property with a rock garden that is a Place of Scenic Beauty; still lived in, so viewed from outside.

places.n: Hoshizuna-no-hama star sand beach, Iriomote (星砂の浜)
places.ad: Uehara, Taketomi, Yaeyama District, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: Small north-shore Iriomote beach whose 'sand' includes millions of star-shaped foraminifera skeletons; snorkelling over the reef straight off the beach.

places.n: Yonekoyaki Shisa Park, Ishigaki (米子焼工房 シーサー園)
places.w: Roadside garden behind the Yonekoyaki pottery workshop crowded with giant, psychedelic, pop-art shisa lion-dog sculptures.
places.nat: 米子焼工房 シーサー園

places.n: Hacksaw Ridge (Maeda Escarpment, 前田高地)
places.w: The Urasoe escarpment where medic Desmond Doss lowered wounded men down the cliff in May 1945; trails lead to Needle Rock and the Doss point above the city.

places.n: Kokusai-dōri (国際通り)
places.w: Naha's 1.6 km main street of shops, cafés, bars and awamori stores, rebuilt so fast after 1945 it was nicknamed the 'Miracle Mile'; the gateway to Makishi market, Tsuboya and the arcades, and the stage for the city's big festivals.

places.n: Kinjō-chō Ishidatami-michi stone-paved road (金城町石畳道)
places.w: About 300 m survive of the c.1522 limestone-paved royal road that ran south from Shuri Castle, winding steeply between old stone walls and red-tiled houses.

places.n: Okinawa Prefectural Museum & Art Museum (沖縄県立博物館・美術館)
places.w: The prefecture's flagship museum in Shintoshin: Ryūkyū history, nature and crafts from prehistory to the US era, with a modern Okinawan art wing.
places.nat: 沖縄県立博物館・美術館

places.n: Sakaemachi Market (栄町市場)
places.w: Showa-era covered market by Asato station: groceries by day, and after dark a warren of tiny bars and izakaya where locals drink on stools in the alleys.

places.n: Sunayama Beach (砂山ビーチ)
places.w: Cove reached over a tall sand dune 4 km north of Hirara, framed by a natural rock arch — one of Miyako's signature beaches.

places.n: Cape Higashi-hennazaki (東平安名崎)
places.w: A 2 km finger of land at Miyako's south-east tip, strewn with tsunami boulders, ending at a 1967 white lighthouse with a 320° ocean panorama.

places.n: Irabu Ōhashi Bridge (伊良部大橋)
places.w: Opened 31 January 2015: at 3,540 m Japan's longest toll-free bridge, arcing over turquoise shallows from Miyako to Irabu Island.

places.n: Valley of Gangala (ガンガラーの谷)
places.w: Collapsed-cave valley of banyan-draped limestone opposite Okinawa World, where remains linked to the 18,000-year-old Minatogawa people were found; visits by guided tour only.

places.n: Bise Fukugi Tree Road (備瀬のフクギ並木)
places.w: Kilometre of sandy lanes in Bise village tunnelled by centuries-old fukugi windbreak trees, five minutes from Churaumi; walk or cycle to Cape Bise.

places.n: Fukushū-en Garden (福州園)
places.w: Walled Chinese garden opened in 1992 for Naha's sister city Fuzhou, built with materials shipped from Fujian — pagoda over a waterfall, ponds and moon gates in old Kume, the Chinese scholars' quarter.

places.n: Hate-no-hama sandbar, Kume Island (ハテの浜)
places.ad: off eastern Kume Island, Kumejima, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: A 7 km ribbon of pure white sand bars in the open sea east of Kume Island, reached only by a 20-minute boat ride — no shade, no buildings, just reef and sky.

places.n: Nago Central Park / Nago Castle Park (名護城公園)
places.w: Hillside park on the old Nago gusuku site — the only place in Okinawa on Japan's list of 100 best cherry-blossom spots (deep-pink kanhi-zakura in late January) — with the Tenjo lookout over Nago Bay.

places.n: Nago Pineapple Park (ナゴパイナップルパーク)
places.w: Kitsch pineapple-themed park on Route 84 with self-driving pineapple carts through the plantation and tastings of pineapple everything.
places.nat: ナゴパイナップルパーク

places.n: DMM Kariyushi Aquarium (DMMかりゆし水族館)
places.ad: iias Okinawa Toyosaki, Toyosaki, Tomigusuku, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: Okinawa's second-largest aquarium, in the iias Toyosaki mall near the airport: projection and AR-enhanced tanks, penguins, and a walkway over a big shark-and-ray tank.

places.n: Ie Island & Mt Gusuku 'Tatchu' (伊江島 城山)
places.w: Flat island a 30-minute ferry from Motobu, dominated by the 172 m rock spire of Gusuku-yama ('Iejima Tatchu') — climb for views back to the Motobu Peninsula.

places.n: Sesoko Island & Sesoko Beach (瀬底島)
places.w: Small bridged island off Motobu with one of the main island area's clearest swimming beaches, facing Minna and Ie islands.

places.n: Mt Yaedake cherry-blossom road (八重岳桜の森公園)
places.w: Japan's first cherry blossoms of the year: about 7,000 deep-pink kanhi-zakura line a 4 km road up the main island's second-highest mountain, with a festival from mid-January.

places.n: Gushikawa Castle Ruins, Itoman (具志川城跡)
places.w: Gusuku perched on sea cliffs at the southern tip of the island, surrounded by sea on three sides — a National Historic Site with sweeping coastal views.

places.n: Itokazu Castle Ruins (糸数城跡)
places.w: Fourteenth-century gusuku at 180 m — the highest castle ruin in the south — its curved limestone walls built to guard Tamagusuku; views over the southern coast.

places.n: Tamagusuku Castle Ruins (玉城城跡)
places.w: The oldest castle on Okinawa Island, said to have been built by the creator goddess Amamikiyo; its arched gate in the natural rock frames the solstice sunrise. National Historic Site.

places.n: Chinen Castle Ruins (知念城跡)
places.w: Compact cliff-top gusuku with a pair of arched stone gates, believed to be the second-oldest castle in the Ryūkyūs; near the sacred Chinen-Ukka spring. National Historic Site.

places.n: Gushikawa Castle Ruins, Kume Island (具志川城跡)
places.w: Fifteenth-century gusuku on a cliff-bound headland in Kume Island's north-west, four low-walled enclosures above the East China Sea; National Historic Site since 1975.

places.n: Tsuboya Pottery Museum (那覇市立壺屋焼物博物館)
places.w: Municipal museum on Yachimun-dōri with some 7,000 pieces — from a 6,700-year-old shard through Ryūkyū-kingdom wares to today's masters — plus a preserved climbing kiln.
places.nat: 那覇市立壺屋焼物博物館

places.n: Tamatorizaki Observation Point, Ishigaki (玉取崎展望台)
places.w: Hilltop platform on Ishigaki's east coast looking over Cape Tamatori, Ibaruma Bay, the hilly Hirakubo peninsula and the reef.

places.n: Yubu Island water-buffalo crossing (由布島)
places.ad: Komi, Taketomi, Yaeyama District, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: Tiny island off Iriomote reached by water-buffalo cart across a shallow sandy strait, often to a sanshin song from the driver; a botanical garden and cafés on the island.

places.n: Iriomote Island jungle & mangroves (西表島)
places.w: Okinawa's second-largest island, about 90 % jungle and mangrove — part of the 2021 UNESCO natural World Heritage site and home of the critically endangered Iriomote cat; explored by river cruise and kayak (Urauchi River, Pinaisara Falls — the prefecture's tallest at 55 m).

places.n: Eef Beach, Kume Island (イーフビーチ)
places.w: Two kilometres of white sand on Kume's east coast, one of Japan's '100 Best Beaches', facing the lagoon and Hate-no-hama.

places.n: Ishigaki Yaima Village (石垣やいま村)
places.w: Open-air village of century-old Yaeyama houses (designated tangible cultural properties) beside a mangrove, with folk-song shows, crafts and the Anparu Shokudō serving Okinawa soba and jūshī.

places.n: Aragusuku Beach, Miyako (新城海岸)
places.w: East-coast reef beach where shallow, glass-clear water puts coral and tropical fish within a few strokes of the sand — Miyako's easy snorkel spot.

places.n: Cape Maeda & the Blue Cave (真栄田岬 青の洞窟)
places.w: Limestone cape on the Onna coast and the island's most popular snorkel and dive entry; swim or boat into the Blue Cave, where light through the sea floor turns the grotto luminous aquamarine.
places.nat: 真栄田岬 青の洞窟

places.n: Emerald Beach, Ocean Expo Park (エメラルドビーチ)
places.ad: Ocean Expo Park, Motobu, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: Three-part beach inside Ocean Expo Park beside Churaumi, one of Japan's '100 best beaches'; free entry and parking, swimming April–October.

places.n: Kariyushi Beach (かりゆしビーチ)
places.w: Resort beach on Nago Bay's western shore with a long swimming season (March–October) and marine activities.

places.n: Okuma Beach (奥間ビーチ)
places.w: Year-round beach resort in Yanbaru, inside the World Natural Heritage north; long a favourite of base families.

places.n: Ginowan Tropical Beach (宜野湾トロピカルビーチ)
places.w: City beach by Ginowan's marina park, a long-time base-family BBQ and swim spot minutes from Naha.
places.nat: 宜野湾トロピカルビーチ

places.n: Toyosaki Chura-Sun Beach (豊崎美らSUNビーチ)
places.w: Long artificial beach on the Toyosaki reclamation near the airport, with BBQ areas and planes overhead.

places.n: Araha Beach, Chatan (アラハビーチ)
places.w: 600 m of white sand in southern Chatan, quieter than Sunset Beach, with lifeguards, BBQ rental and water sports; swimming April–October.

places.n: Azama Sun Sun Beach (あざまサンサンビーチ)
places.w: Shallow family beach by Azama port (the ferry to Kudaka), fringed with lawns, with a beach house and reservable BBQ sets.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — The Aquatope on White Sand (白い砂のアクアトープ, 2021) — the beach's wooden swing appears in the series; Nanjō named an 'Anime Pilgrimage 88' site (Ryukyu Shimpo entry-1580769) · Family beach
places.nat: あざまサンサンビーチ

places.n: Mibaru Beach & glass-bottom boats (新原ビーチ)
places.w: Two kilometres of natural sand on the south-east coast, launch point for glass-bottom boats over the reef.

places.n: Toguchi Beach, Yomitan (渡具知ビーチ) — US landing beach
places.w: Beach at the mouth of the Hija River where US Marines came ashore on 1 April 1945; now a quiet park beach.

places.n: Aharen Beach, Tokashiki Island (阿波連ビーチ)
places.w: Tokashiki's main beach in the Kerama Islands National Park: a long curve of white sand and 'Kerama blue' reef water, with a campground nearby.

places.n: Cape Irizaki, Yonaguni — Japan's westernmost point (西崎)
places.w: Cliff-ringed cape at the west tip of Yonaguni, the last place in Japan to see the sunset: lighthouse, lookout and the 'westernmost point of Japan' monument; Taiwan, 107 km away, is visible on clear days.

places.n: Yonaguni Monument underwater formation (与那国島海底地形)
places.w: Terraced underwater rock formation found by a diver in 1986 off Yonaguni's south coast — natural or man-made is still debated; reached on dive and glass-bottom boat trips.

places.n: Mamoru-kun police-officer figures, Miyako (宮古島まもる君)
places.w: Life-size painted policeman figures posted at Miyako crossings by the traffic-safety association since the 1990s — now the island's cult mascot.

places.n: Benzaitendō & Enkaku-ji, Shuri (弁財天堂・円覚寺跡)
places.ad: Shuri Castle Park, Shuri, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: Islet hall to the goddess of sea voyages in Enkan-chi pond, opposite the gate of Enkaku-ji — the royal family temple whose National Treasures were lost in 1945.

places.n: Nirai Kanai Bridge overlook (ニライカナイ橋)
places.w: A sweeping U-shaped road bridge that switchbacks down the Chinen hillside with the Pacific and Kudaka Island ahead — best seen from the tunnel-top viewpoint. It appears in the 2021 anime 'The Aquatope on White Sand', which earned Nanjō a place among the Anime Tourism Association's 88 anime pilgrimage sites.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — The Aquatope on White Sand (白い砂のアクアトープ, 2021) — bridge shown in the series; Nanjō named an 'Anime Pilgrimage 88' site · Coastal bridge & viewpoint (anime pilgrimage)

places.n: Kouri Ōhashi Bridge & Kouri Island (古宇利大橋・古宇利島)
places.w: The 1,960 m toll-free bridge (2005) from Yagaji Island across emerald shallows to Kouri, the 'Island of Love' — one of Okinawa's signature drives, with beaches, Heart Rock and garlic-shrimp trucks at the far end.
places.nat: 古宇利大橋・古宇利島

places.n: Ama Beach, Zamami Island (阿真ビーチ)
places.w: The quieter of Zamami's two main beaches, on the southwest shore facing the uninhabited islets of Gahi and Agenashiku; sea turtles graze offshore.

places.n: Takatsukiyama Observatory, Zamami (高月山展望台)
places.w: Hilltop lookout over Zamami village, Furuzamami Beach and the scattered Kerama islands — the classic Kerama Blue panorama.

places.n: Pokémon Center Okinawa, Aeon Mall Okinawa Rycom (ポケモンセンターオキナワ)
places.ad: Aeon Mall Okinawa Rycom 1F, 1 Raikamu, Kitanakagusuku, Okinawa 901-2306, Japan
places.w: Okinawa's first Pokémon Center (opened 11 Aug 2022, Japan's 16th), themed on the island's nature: Pikachu and Arcanine greet you at the entrance, with Okinawa-only goods and a video zone. Pair it with a hunt for the prefecture's 16 Pokémon manhole 'Poké Lids'.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Pokémon — the prefecture's only Pokémon Center, with Okinawa-exclusive merchandise · Pokémon flagship store
places.nat: ポケモンセンターオキナワ

places.n: Sueyoshi-gū Shrine & Sueyoshi Park (末吉宮)
places.w: One of the Eight Shrines of the Ryūkyū Kingdom, perched on a forested limestone ridge in Sueyoshi Park; a stone path climbs through jungle to the rebuilt hall — a quiet counterpoint to Shuri Castle.

places.n: Sōgen-ji Stone Gate (崇元寺石門)
places.w: The surviving stone gate of the Ryūkyū royal temple founded in 1527, where all who entered — even the king — had to dismount; the temple was destroyed in WWII but the gate was restored and has been an Important Cultural Property since 1972, fronting a small park.
places.k: Ryukyu royal temple gate (Important Cultural Property)

places.n: Ryūtan Pond, Shuri (龍潭)
places.ad: Shuri Castle Park, Shuri, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: The 'Dragon Depths' pond below Shuri Castle, dug in 1427 under King Shō Hashi by the official Kaiki to entertain Chinese envoys; the classic reflection view of the castle walls.

places.n: Okinawa Karate Kaikan (沖縄空手会館)
places.w: The prefecture's home of karate, opened March 2017 on a 3.8 ha site near Naha Airport: a museum on the art's Okinawan origins, training dojo and the ceremonial Shureikan hall.

places.n: Michi-no-Eki Kadena observation deck (道の駅かでな)
places.w: Roadside station beside Kadena Air Base whose rooftop observation deck looks straight across the runway — the place locals and plane-spotters watch fighter jets take off and land; Mapple ranks it Okinawa's No. 3 michi-no-eki.

places.n: Ishigaki-jima Limestone Cave (石垣島鍾乳洞)
places.w: Japan's southernmost show cave: 3.2 km of limestone formed over some 200,000 years in southern Ishigaki, with a lit walkway through the formations.

places.n: Nishihama Beach, Hateruma Island (ニシ浜)
places.ad: Hateruma, Taketomi, Yaeyama District, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: The beach that gave its name to 'Hateruma Blue' — powder-white sand and impossibly saturated turquoise water on Japan's southernmost inhabited island; stay overnight for the star-field sky.

places.n: 17END, Shimoji Island (17エンド)
places.w: The shallows off the end of Shimoji Airport's runway 17, where a sandbar appears at low tide in remarkably clear turquoise water — about 15–20 minutes' drive from Miyako over the Irabu Bridge.

places.n: Cape Chinen Park (知念岬公園)
places.w: A grassy clifftop park at the tip of Chinen Cape, about 40 m above the sea, with a roughly 250-degree view over the reef toward Kudaka and Komaka islands, a short walk from Sefa-utaki. It is one of the settings of the 2021 anime 'The Aquatope on White Sand', the reason the Anime Tourism Association named Nanjō one of its '88 Anime Pilgrimage' sites.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — The Aquatope on White Sand (白い砂のアクアトープ, 2021) — cape park shown in the series; Nanjō is an Anime Tourism '88' site · Cape viewpoint (anime pilgrimage)

places.n: Okitsura pilgrimage — Gushikawa, Uruma (沖ツラ聖地 具志川公民館・具志川ビーチ)
places.ad: 381 Gushikawa, Uruma, Okinawa, Japan (Gushikawa Community Hall 具志川公民館)
places.w: The residential Gushikawa district of Uruma is the main real-world setting of the anime 'Fall in Love with Okinawa Dialect' (沖ツラ). Gushikawa Beach appears in episode 2 and other walk-to-school scenes, and pilgrims start from the Gushikawa Community Hall, which hands out Uruma's official location map and has one of three Okitsura manhole covers (the others are at KIN Sunrise Beach and Michi-no-Eki Ginoza).
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Fall in Love with Okinawa Dialect (沖縄で好きになった子が方言すぎてツラすぎる / 沖ツラ, 2025 anime) — set in Gushikawa, Uruma; official city location map and collab manhole · Anime pilgrimage neighbourhood
places.nat: 沖ツラ聖地 具志川公民館・具志川ビーチ

places.n: Tomari International Cemetery (泊外人墓地)
places.ad: Tomari, Naha, Okinawa (north shore of Tomari Port)
places.w: A small walled cemetery on the north bank of Tomari Port holding about 22 foreigners from the 18th to early 20th centuries and some 300 post-war burials, with a monument to Commodore Perry's 1853 landing. Its oldest Western grave, of the British sailor 'WM HARES', is dated 1816.
places.k: Historic foreigners' cemetery & Perry landing monument

places.n: Naminoue Beach & Naminoue Umisora Park (波の上ビーチ・波の上うみそら公園)
places.w: Naha's only city beach, sitting below the cliff-top Naminoue Shrine, with free entry and swimming from mid-April to October. The adjoining Umisora Park's enclosed man-made bay is a favourite with people learning to dive.
places.nat: 波の上ビーチ・波の上うみそら公園

places.n: Shuri Kannondō (Jigen-in) (首里観音堂 慈眼院)
places.w: A Rinzai Zen temple at the end of the old royal road out of Shuri, founded in 1618 by King Shō Kyū to give thanks for the safe return of his son (later King Shō Hō) from Satsuma captivity, and rebuilt after the Battle of Okinawa. Envoys bound for Edo prayed here for a safe voyage; free to visit.
places.k: Thousand-armed Kannon temple of the Ryūkyū kings
places.nat: 首里観音堂 慈眼院

places.n: Kakazu Ridge — Kakazu Takadai Park (嘉数高台公園)
places.w: One of the fiercest battlefields of the 1945 Battle of Okinawa: US forces attacked Kakazu Ridge on 9 April 1945 and needed about 15 days to take it, with thousands dead on both sides. Today a hilltop park with a globe-shaped observation deck looking over Futenma Air Station and toward the Maeda Escarpment, plus surviving pillboxes.

places.n: Haebaru Army Hospital Shelter No. 20 (南風原陸軍病院壕 20号壕)
places.w: Hand-dug tunnel used as a ward of the Okinawa Army Hospital in 1945, where the Himeyuri student nurses were first assigned before the retreat south. Guided visits by appointment through the Haebaru Town Culture Center (¥300).
places.nat: 南風原陸軍病院壕 20号壕

places.n: Minatogawa Stateside Town (港川ステイツサイドタウン)
places.w: A neighbourhood of 1950s–60s white single-storey 'foreign houses' built for US military families, now converted into cafés, bakeries, galleries and shops. Lanes are named after US states (Oregon, Arizona, Michigan, Kansas and more); about 5 minutes' walk from the Minatogawa bus stop.
places.nat: 港川ステイツサイドタウン

places.n: Chibichiri Gama (チビチリガマ)
places.w: A natural cave near the US landing beaches where, in April 1945, 140 villagers sheltered as American forces approached and 83 died in a forced mass suicide. A memorial stands at the mouth; the cave itself is closed to entry out of respect, and memorial services are held each spring.

places.n: Nakamura House (中村家住宅)
places.w: A wealthy farmer's homestead built in the 1720s — the island's prime surviving example of early-modern Okinawan domestic architecture, with red-tiled roofs, a coral-stone wall and fukugi-tree windbreak; a National Important Cultural Property near Nakagusuku Castle.

places.n: Kudaka Island (久高島)
places.w: The 'island of the gods', 5.3 km off Cape Chinen: in Ryūkyū belief the creator goddess Amamikyo descended here, and kings once made pilgrimage to it. A slender 1.38 km² island reached by ferry from Azama port, explored by bicycle; some sacred groves are off-limits.

places.n: Urasoe Yōdore Royal Mausoleum & Urasoe Castle ruins (浦添ようどれ・浦添城跡)
places.w: Cliffside royal tombs carved under King Eiso in 1261, below the ridge of Urasoe Castle, seat of the early Chūzan kings. The ridge was a Japanese defensive line in 1945 and the tombs, badly damaged, were later restored; free entry and parking, ~15 min walk from Urasoe-Maeda monorail station.
places.nat: 浦添ようどれ・浦添城跡

places.n: Plaza House Shopping Center (プラザハウス ショッピングセンター)
places.w: Billed as Japan's first shopping center, opened in 1954 to serve officers and families of the nearby US Ryukyu Command HQ. Its mid-century three-storey atrium and single-storey arcade survive, now holding an international food market, cafés, bakeries, interiors stores and Okinawan crafts; it appears in the Agency for Cultural Affairs' survey of Okinawa's modern architecture.
places.nat: プラザハウス ショッピングセンター

places.n: Okinawa Zoo & Museum — Okinawa Kodomo no Kuni (沖縄こどもの国)
places.w: Japan's southernmost zoo and the only one in the prefecture, reopened in 2004 with a child-focused layout: Nature Land (the zoo, with Yanbaru and Okinawan native species), the three-storey hands-on Wonder Museum and a Children's Center with petting animals.

places.n: Pinaisara Falls, Iriomote (ピナイサーラの滝)
places.w: Okinawa Prefecture's highest waterfall — a 54 m drop on the Hinai River, reached by kayaking the Hinai mangroves and a jungle trail inside Iriomote-Ishigaki National Park.

places.n: Urauchi River & Mariyudu Falls, Iriomote (浦内川・マリユドゥの滝)
places.w: Okinawa's longest river: a boat cruise up the mangrove-lined Urauchi, then a jungle walk to Mariyudu Falls, a two-tier fall selected among Japan's 100 best waterfalls.
places.k: River cruise to a top-100 waterfall
places.nat: 浦内川・マリユドゥの滝

places.n: Cape Hirakubo & lighthouse, Ishigaki (平久保崎)
places.w: The northern tip of Ishigaki's Hirakubo Peninsula; from the white lighthouse the Pacific lies on one side and the East China Sea on the other.

places.n: Cape Agarizaki, Yonaguni (東崎)
places.w: Cliff-top cape at Yonaguni's eastern end, grazed by Yonaguni horses, with views across to Iriomote on clear days.

places.n: Kondoi Beach, Taketomi Island (コンドイ浜)
places.w: Taketomi's west-coast swimming beach: white sand and a long, shallow emerald lagoon calm enough for small children; reached by rental bicycle from the village.

places.n: Neo Park Okinawa, Nago (ネオパークオキナワ)
places.w: Nago's municipal wildlife and botanical park (opened December 1992): about 100 species in free-roaming Africa, Amazon and Oceania zones, circled by a small light railway.

places.n: Gesashi Bay mangroves, Higashi (慶佐次湾のヒルギ林)
places.w: The second-largest mangrove forest on Okinawa's main island — about 10 ha along the Gesashi River estuary, explored by boardwalk or guided kayak.

places.n: Nanjō City Regional Products Hall — Midori no Yakata Sēfā (南城市地域物産館 緑の館・セーファ)
places.w: The roadside products hall at the foot of Sēfa-utaki, with about 200 local souvenirs downstairs and a restaurant and café upstairs. It is the official Aquatope pilgrimage base: Nanjō keeps its Anime Tourism Association '88 Anime Pilgrimage' certification plate and goshuin-style memorial stamp here.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — The Aquatope on White Sand (2021) — holds Nanjō's Anime Tourism '88' certification plate and pilgrimage stamp · Aquatope pilgrimage stamp & plate
places.nat: 南城市地域物産館 緑の館・セーファ

places.n: Nishihara Kira Kira Beach (西原きらきらビーチ)
places.ad: Agarizaki, Nishihara, Nakagami District, Okinawa, Japan (Creed Nishihara Marine Park)
places.w: A 550 m man-made beach inside Creed Nishihara Marine Park on the east coast, with free entry and parking, sports fields, a barbecue area and beach-volleyball courts. It is the venue of the climactic tournament in the beach-volleyball anime 'Harukana Receive' (2018).
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Harukana Receive (はるかなレシーブ, 2018) — real venue of the series' final beach-volleyball tournament · Beach-volleyball anime setting

places.n: Sugar Loaf Hill (シュガーローフ / 安里52高地)
places.w: The low hill the US Marines called Sugar Loaf and the Japanese 'Asato Hill 52', locally Kerama-chiiji, was fought over by the 6th Marine Division and the Japanese 32nd Army in May 1945. Today it is the Asato reservoir park beside Omoromachi monorail station, with an inscribed marker amid the new city centre.
places.k: Battle of Okinawa hill in the middle of Shintoshin
places.nat: シュガーローフ / 安里52高地

places.n: Great Akagi Trees of Shuri Kinjō (首里金城の大アカギ)
places.w: A grove of six huge akagi (Bischofia) trees and one Ryūkyū hackberry behind the Uchikanagusuku shrine just off the Kinjō-chō stone road, designated a national Natural Monument in 1972; the largest is 5.2 m round and 13 m tall. No other such grove of giant akagi survives in a settled area of Okinawa.
places.k: National Natural Monument grove off the stone road

places.n: Kayauchi Banta cliff, Kunigami (茅打バンタ)
places.w: A ~100 m sheer cliff and lookout near the island's northern tip, inside Yanbaru National Park; the name ('banta' = cliff) comes from the tale that a bundle of thatch thrown over the edge was torn apart by the wind.

places.n: Senaga Island & Umikaji Terrace, Tomigusuku (瀬長島ウミカジテラス)
places.w: A small island ~600 m off the southern west coast and 1.5 km south of Naha Airport, returned by the US military in 1977; since summer 2015 its slope is lined with the white, Mediterranean-style shops and cafés of Umikaji Terrace, with planes landing overhead and sunset views.
places.nat: 瀬長島ウミカジテラス

places.n: Cape Kyan & the Peace Tower, Itoman (喜屋武岬)
places.w: The south-western tip of the main island, 10–20 m cliffs where the Pacific meets the East China Sea; this coast saw the last desperate fighting of the Battle of Okinawa, and the 1969 Peace Tower memorial stands at the point, inside Okinawa Senseki Quasi-National Park.

places.n: Todoroki Falls Park, Nago (轟の滝)
places.w: A roughly 28 m waterfall a five-minute drive inland from Route 58, designated a prefectural scenic spot; a small managed park (open 9–18, ¥200) with stream play and barbecue areas.

places.n: Shimashi Ōzato Castle Ruins, Nanjō (島添大里城跡)
places.ad: Ōzato, Ōzato, Nanjō, Okinawa, Japan (Ōzato Castle Ruins Park)
places.w: A 14th-century gusuku on the eastern end of a ~150 m limestone ridge, seat of the Shimashi-Ōzato lords until Shō Hashi took it in 1402 on his way to unifying the Ryūkyū Kingdom; designated a National Historic Site in 2012.

places.n: Uegusuku Castle Ruins, Kume Island (宇江城城跡)
places.w: Gusuku ruins on the 310 m summit of Uegusuku-dake — the highest castle site in Okinawa Prefecture — with a 360-degree view over almost the whole of Kume Island. Free. Designated a National Historic Site in 2009.

places.n: Toguchi-no-hama Beach, Irabu Island (渡口の浜)
places.w: An 800 m gently curving arc of fine white sand on south-west Irabu, renowned across Okinawa for its powdery sand and clear water, looking across to Miyako and Kurima islands; counted among Irabu's finest beaches.

places.n: Takanazaki & Japan's Southernmost Point Monument, Hateruma (高那崎・日本最南端の碑)
places.ad: Hateruma Island, Taketomi, Yaeyama, Okinawa (south tip; ~10 min by car from Hateruma port)
places.w: Kilometre-long limestone cliffs at the southern tip of Hateruma, Japan's southernmost inhabited island, where a monument to the southernmost point (erected 1970) stands beside Taketomi Town's peace monument and a path of stones from every prefecture.
places.nat: 高那崎・日本最南端の碑

places.n: KIN Sunrise Beach (KINサンライズビーチ海浜公園)
places.ad: 10819-4 Kin, Kin Town, Kunigami District, Okinawa 904-1201, Japan
places.w: An 800 m long-beach seaside park in Kin, listed by the OCVB film office as a location. It is one of the three official pilgrimage stops for the manga and anime 'Okitsura': one of the series' manhole covers was installed here, and the Kin Bay council ran its Okitsura collaboration campaign from the park's management building. The campaign art shows the heroines eating taco rice, the dish that started in Kin, against this beach.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Okitsura (沖縄で好きになった子が方言すぎてツラすぎる, anime 2025) — official Okitsura manhole + Kan-Kin-Bay council collab campaign site · Okitsura manhole & collab beach
places.nat: KINサンライズビーチ海浜公園

places.n: Michi-no-Eki Ginoza (道の駅ぎのざ)
places.ad: 1633 Kanna, Ginoza Village, Kunigami District, Okinawa 904-1304, Japan
places.w: A roadside station on Route 329, the first on Okinawa's east coast. It is known for its water-play plaza and giant slide, and an All About 2025 survey ranked it second among Okinawa roadside stations to visit with children. One of the three official Okitsura manhole covers, showing the heroines and Ginoza's mascot Gī-no-kun, was installed here as part of the Kin Bay council's pilgrimage campaign.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Okitsura (沖縄で好きになった子が方言すぎてツラすぎる, anime 2025) — official Okitsura manhole (with Ginoza mascot Gī-no-kun) · Okitsura manhole at a family roadside station

places.n: Sakima Art Museum (佐喜眞美術館)
places.w: Private museum opened in 1994 on land reclaimed from a corner of US Marine Corps Air Station Futenma. Its centrepiece is Iri and Toshi Maruki's 4 × 8.5 m 'Battle of Okinawa' panel, painted from survivors' testimony by the artists of the Hiroshima Panels.
places.k: The Marukis' Battle of Okinawa mural beside Futenma

places.n: Futenma-gū Shrine & cave (普天満宮)
places.w: One of the Ryūkyū Eight Shrines granted special status by the kingdom; it began as worship of an indigenous deity in its cave, with Kumano Gongen enshrined in the mid-15th century. The 280 m limestone cave behind the hall, where 3,000-year-old artefacts were excavated, is a Ginowan city Place of Scenic Beauty and can be visited.
places.k: Ryūkyū Eight Shrines member with a sacred cave

places.n: Southeast Botanical Gardens (東南植物楽園)
places.w: One of Japan's largest outdoor botanical gardens, with about 1,300 species and over 50,000 plants, and a nationally Registered Monument. Seasonal night illuminations draw crowds in winter.

places.n: Koza Music Town (コザ・ミュージックタウン)
places.w: Okinawa City's 'town of music' hub, opened in 2007 at the Koza crossroads as part of the city's music-led regeneration: the Ongaku Ichiba (Music Town Ongaku Ichiba) live hall, studios and a music plaza that hosts events tied to the All-Island Eisa Festival.
places.k: Hub of Koza's rock and min'yō scene
places.nat: コザ・ミュージックタウン

places.n: Busena Marine Park Underwater Observatory, Nago (ブセナ海中公園 海中展望塔)
places.w: Opened in 1970 at the tip of Busena Cape, the observatory stands 170 m offshore at the end of a footbridge; a spiral stair descends to round windows 5 m below the surface for watching reef fish. Glass-bottom boats run from the same park.
places.k: Walk down to the reef 5 m underwater
places.nat: ブセナ海中公園 海中展望塔

places.n: Ryukyu Mura, Onna (琉球村)
places.w: A hands-on culture village of old Okinawan farmhouses moved here from around the islands, recreating pre-war village life; visitors try indigo dyeing, pottery, weaving and bingata stencil-dyeing and watch Ryukyuan performing-arts shows.

places.n: Arakaki Family Residence, Tsuboya (新垣家住宅)
places.w: The only surviving 18th-century Tsuboya potter's compound — red-tiled main house, workshop, climbing kiln (the former royal 'Higashi-nu-kama') and stone pigsty-toilet — designated an Important Cultural Property in 2002.
places.k: Important Cultural Property · Tsuboya potter's house & climbing kiln

places.n: Tsushima Maru Memorial Museum (対馬丸記念館)
places.w: Museum (opened 22 Aug 2004) on the 1944 sinking of the evacuation ship Tsushima Maru, in which hundreds of Okinawan schoolchildren died; run by the Tsushima Maru Memorial Association beside Gokoku-ji and Naminoue.

places.n: Mekaru Tomb Site, Shintoshin (銘苅墓跡群)
places.ad: Mekaru 2-chōme (hill opposite the Naha City Fire Department HQ), Naha, Okinawa
places.w: National Historic Site (2007): a hillside necropolis of 330+ tombs spanning the Gusuku era through the Ryūkyū Kingdom to Meiji, the oldest from the 14th–15th c.; its largest turtleback tomb is 22 m wide and 30 m deep. Survived the build-out of Naha Shintoshin.
places.k: National Historic Site · 330 Ryūkyū tombs in the new city centre

places.n: Gokoku-ji Temple, Naminoue (護国寺)
places.w: Shingon temple founded in 1367 beside Naminoue Shrine, once the Ryūkyū Kingdom's royal prayer temple and head of Shingon in the kingdom. Missionary Bernard Bettelheim occupied it 1846–1853, and its 1465 bell was given to Commodore Perry (long kept at Annapolis).
places.k: Ryūkyū royal temple · Bettelheim & Perry's bell

places.n: Inazaki Observatory, Zamami (稲崎展望台)
places.ad: Northern tip of Zamami Island, Zamami-son, Shimajiri District, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: Hilltop lookout on Zamami's north side, about an hour's walk from the port; on clear days Aguni, Tonaki and Kume islands are visible, and it is the best spot for watching humpback whales, which frequent these waters December–April. Part of Keramashotō National Park.

places.n: Konpaku-no-tō memorial, Itoman (魂魄の塔)
places.w: The first war memorial raised after the Battle of Okinawa, built by residents themselves in February 1946 from gathered remains; enshrining some 35,000 people, it is the largest in the prefecture, and families gather here at dawn every Irei-no-hi (23 June).

places.n: Poké Lid — Growlithe over Mihama fireworks, Depot Island Boardwalk, Chatan (ポケふた ガーディ 北谷町美浜)
places.ad: Depot Island Boardwalk (seaside), 9-1 Mihama, Chatan Town, Okinawa 904-0115, Japan
places.w: A Pokémon manhole cover installed in August 2025 at the seaside boardwalk of Depot Island in Mihama. It shows Growlithe, Okinawa's 'support Pokémon', against American Village's night skyline and fireworks. It sits just before the boardwalk steps, which is also a popular fireworks-viewing spot. It is one of four Growlithe lids the Pokémon Company gave to Okinawan towns in 2025.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Pokémon (Poké Lids / Pokémon Local Acts) — Growlithe, Okinawa's 'support Pokémon', over American Village fireworks · Pokémon manhole on the boardwalk
places.nat: ポケふた ガーディ 北谷町美浜

places.n: Poké Lid — Solrock & Skiploom, Kumiodori Park, Urasoe (ポケふた ソルロック×ポポッコ 組踊公園)
places.ad: Kumiodori Park (south plaza of the National Theatre Okinawa), 4-14-1 Jitchaku, Urasoe, Okinawa 901-2122, Japan
places.w: Urasoe's Pokémon manhole cover was set into Kumiodori Park, next to the National Theatre Okinawa, in February 2022. That made Urasoe the fifth city in the prefecture with a Poké Lid. Solrock stands for the sun (tida), Urasoe's symbol, and Skiploom carries yellow flowers in the colour of the city flower. It is on the OCVB 'Flying Pikachu' Poké Lid trail.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Pokémon (Poké Lids / Pokémon Local Acts) — Solrock (Urasoe's sun, tida) and Skiploom, beside the home of kumiodori · Pokémon manhole at the National Theatre
places.nat: ポケふた ソルロック×ポポッコ 組踊公園

places.n: Poké Lid — Tauros & Katsuren Castle, Ishikawa Sports Grounds, Uruma (ポケふた ケンタロス×勝連城跡 石川運動広場)
places.ad: Entrance of Ishikawa Sports Grounds, (石川運動広場), 2316 Ishikawa, Uruma, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: Uruma's Pokémon manhole cover shows a charging Tauros, a nod to the city's bullfighting (tōgyū) culture, with the UNESCO-listed Katsuren Castle ruins behind it. It was installed at the entrance of the Ishikawa Sports Grounds as part of Pokémon's 'Flying Pikachu Project' and is on the OCVB Poké Lid trail.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Pokémon (Poké Lids / Flying Pikachu Project) — Tauros for Uruma's bullfighting culture, with Katsuren Castle · Pokémon bullfight manhole
places.nat: ポケふた ケンタロス×勝連城跡 石川運動広場

places.n: Poké Lid — Arcanine, Tenbusu Plaza, Kokusai-dōri (ポケふた ウインディ てんぶす広場)
places.ad: Tenbusu Plaza (Tenbusu Naha), 3-2 Makishi, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: Naha's original Pokémon manhole cover, an Arcanine design on the OCVB 'Flying Pikachu' Poké Lid trail, set in Tenbusu Plaza on Kokusai-dōri. In April 2026 a photo of it covered by pipe chairs during an event drew more than 24 million views. Naha City then said it was considering moving the lid and was in talks with The Pokémon Company. Check it is still here before you go.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Pokémon (Poké Lids / Flying Pikachu Project) — Naha's Arcanine lid; went viral in 2026 when buried under event chairs (relocation under review) · Viral Pokémon manhole on Kokusai-dōri
places.nat: ポケふた ウインディ てんぶす広場

places.n: Kume Shiseibyō Confucius Temple (久米至聖廟)
places.w: Naha's Confucian temple, a centre of Chinese learning for the Ryūkyū Kingdom since the original was built in 1671–75; its precinct holds the Meirindō, Okinawa's first public school. Rebuilt in Kume in 2013 beside Fukushū-en, on the old Chinese-émigré Kume village.
places.k: The Ryūkyū Kingdom's Confucian temple, in old Kume village

places.n: Naha City Museum of History (那覇市歴史博物館) — CLOSED
places.ad: Palette Kumoji 4F, 1-1-1 Kumoji, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: Opened in 2006 to show the National Treasure 'Materials related to the Shō Family of Ryūkyū Kings' (1,166 documents and 85 art objects, including the royal crown). It closed on 31 August 2025; the treasures are due to be shown at the former Nakagusuku Udun site, opening date not yet set.
places.k: Closed Aug 2025 — home of the Shō royal National Treasures

places.n: Heiwa-dōri Shopping Arcade (平和通り商店街)
places.w: Covered arcade of around 200 shops branching off Kokusai-dōri toward Makishi Public Market, nicknamed the 'labyrinth arcade'. Named 'Peace Street' by public competition in 1951 after the Heiwa-kan cinema at its mouth; a new generation of shop owners has revived it since the 2000s.

places.n: Bin-nu-utaki / Bengadake Sacred Grove (弁之御嶽・弁ヶ嶽)
places.w: At 165.7 m the highest point in Naha, about 1 km east of Shuri Castle. In the Ryūkyū Kingdom it was a state place of worship where the king, or his envoy, prayed for his health and the nation's peace; designated a National Historic Site as 'Bin-nu-utaki' on 15 October 2018.
places.k: Naha's highest hill, a royal prayer site behind Shuri

places.n: Okinawa Gokoku Shrine, Onoyama Park (沖縄県護国神社)
places.ad: Onoyama Park, Ōnoyama-chō, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: The prefecture's gokoku shrine for its war dead, set inside Onoyama Park on an islet in the Kokuba River. One of Okinawa's most-visited shrines for hatsumōde New Year prayers.
places.k: Okinawa's shrine to the war dead, a top New Year spot

places.n: Mie Gusuku Fort (三重城)
places.w: Gusuku built by King Shō Sei in 1546 on the north mouth of Naha harbour, paired with Yarazamori Gusuku to guard the port and town. A coast-guard watchtower stands on it today, but the stone site is open to the public as a sea-view lookout.
places.k: 1546 harbour fort, now a quiet sunset lookout

places.n: Shuri Ryusen bingata & coral-dye studio (首里琉染)
places.w: Bingata workshop and shop five minutes' walk from Shuri Castle Park, selling bingata and its own 'coral-dye' (sango-zome) textiles. Upstairs visitors can try coral dyeing (about 50 minutes) and watch artisans dyeing in the third-floor studio.
places.k: Try Ryūkyū coral-dyeing beside Shuri Castle

places.n: Yogi Park cherry blossoms (与儀公園)
places.w: City park that is Naha's best-known cherry-blossom spot, with more than 400 Kanhizakura (Taiwan cherry) trees. They flower among Japan's earliest, and the Naha Cherry Blossom Festival is held here in early February.

places.n: Naha Traditional Arts & Crafts Center, Tenbusu Naha (那覇市伝統工芸館)
places.ad: Tenbusu Naha 2F, 3-2-10 Makishi, Naha, Okinawa 900-0013, Japan
places.w: City-run crafts centre on Kokusai-dōri with exhibition rooms, a shop and hands-on workshops for five Naha traditional crafts, including Ryūkyū glass, bingata, Shuri-ori weaving, lacquerware and Tsuboya pottery. Featured on the OCVB's Naha traditional-crafts walking course.
places.k: Try five Naha crafts on Kokusai-dōri

places.n: Poké Lid — Emolga & Pikipek at Hinpun Gajumaru, Nago (ポケふた エモンガ×ツツケラ ひんぷんガジュマル)
places.ad: Gajumaru Ryokuchi Park, 2-321-3 Gusuku, Nago, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: A Pokémon manhole cover (Poké Lid) set beside Nago's Hinpun Gajumaru, the 240-plus-year-old national-monument banyan on Nago's main street. It shows Emolga and Pikipek playing in the tree. Nago installed it in Gajumaru Ryokuchi Park on 15 February 2022, and it is on the OCVB Poké Lid trail.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Pokémon (Poké Lids) — Emolga & Pikipek playing in the Hinpun Gajumaru, Nago's symbol; northern stop on the Okinawa Poké Lid trail · Pokémon manhole under Nago's great banyan
places.nat: ポケふた エモンガ×ツツケラ ひんぷんガジュマル

places.n: Poké Lid — Wartortle & Sandygast, Michi-no-Eki Itoman (ポケふた カメール×スナバァ 道の駅いとまん)
places.ad: Michi-no-Eki Itoman (covered eating area), 4-19-1 Nishizaki-chō, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: A Pokémon manhole cover showing Wartortle and Sandygast on an Itoman sandy beach. It is set inside the covered eating area of Michi-no-Eki Itoman, the roadside station that houses the fishermen's co-op fish market. It is one of three south-Okinawa lids unveiled together for Itoman, Tomigusuku and Nanjō, and is on the OCVB Poké Lid trail.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Pokémon (Poké Lids) — Wartortle with Sandygast on Itoman's beach; the southern-Okinawa Poké Lid set (Itoman/Tomigusuku/Nanjō) · Pokémon manhole at the fish-market roadside station
places.nat: ポケふた カメール×スナバァ 道の駅いとまん

places.n: Poké Lid — Axew & Jangmo-o on a Hārī boat, Michi-no-Eki Toyosaki (ポケふた キバゴ×ジャラコ 道の駅豊崎)
places.ad: Michi-no-Eki Toyosaki, 3-39 Toyosaki, Tomigusuku, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: Tomigusuku's Pokémon manhole cover shows Axew and Jangmo-o riding a dragon boat, a nod to the city's claim to be the birthplace of the Hārī boat race. It sits at Michi-no-Eki Toyosaki, the roadside station near Naha Airport. It was installed in the same south-Okinawa set as the Itoman and Nanjō lids, and is on the OCVB Poké Lid trail.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Pokémon (Poké Lids) — Axew & Jangmo-o on a Hārī dragon boat, Tomigusuku's lid in the southern-Okinawa set · Pokémon manhole near the airport
places.nat: ポケふた キバゴ×ジャラコ 道の駅豊崎

places.n: Nishi-sanbashi West Pier, Taketomi Island (西桟橋)
places.ad: 207 Taketomi, Taketomi Town, Yaeyama District, Okinawa 907-1101, Japan
places.w: A 105 m limestone-and-concrete pier built in 1938 on Taketomi's west coast. Islanders once sailed from here to farm rice paddies on Iriomote. It went out of use around 1971 and was registered as a Tangible Cultural Property in 2005. It is now the island's sunset spot, and it is the key-visual location of the film 'Non Non Biyori Vacation', which the Anime Tourism Association listed in its '88 Anime Pilgrimage Sites' from 2019 to 2024.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Non Non Biyori Vacation (2018 film) — the West Pier is the film's key visual; Anime Tourism 88 Yaeyama/Taketomi entry 2019–2024 · Sunset pier and Non Non Biyori key visual

places.n: Kouri Ocean Tower, Kouri Island (古宇利オーシャンタワー)
places.w: A white observation tower on Kouri Island whose deck stands 82 m above sea level, looking over the cobalt sea and the Kouri Ōhashi bridge; Okinawa Traveler's northern-cafés feature recommends a meal there with the view. Listed by the OCVB and the Nakijin Village tourism association.
places.k: 82 m above the sea, looking down the Kouri bridge
places.nat: 古宇利オーシャンタワー

places.n: Shikina-gū Shrine (識名宮)
places.w: One of the Ryūkyū Hassha, the eight shrines given royal patronage by the Ryūkyū Kingdom, near Shikinaen in Hantagawa. Its origin story centres on a sacred cave, which the shrine opens to visitors on the 1st and 15th of each month.
places.k: Royal-patronage shrine of the Ryūkyū Eight, with a sacred cave

places.n: Okinogū Shrine, Onoyama Park (沖宮)
places.w: One of the Ryūkyū Hassha, dedicated to Kumano Gongen and long prayed to for safe voyages by tribute ships. Founded beside Naha harbour (per the 1713 Ryūkyū-koku Yuraiki), designated a National Treasure in 1935, destroyed in 1945, re-established in 1961 and moved to Onoyama Park in 1975.
places.k: Ryūkyū's harbour shrine for safe voyages, rebuilt in Onoyama Park

places.n: Asato Hachimangū Shrine (安里八幡宮)
places.w: One of the Ryūkyū Hassha, founded in the Tianshun era (1457–64) and enshrining Emperor Ōjin, Empress Jingū and Tamayori-hime; the only Hachiman shrine among the eight. A short walk from Asato and Omoromachi stations.

places.n: Ameku-gū Shrine, Tomari (天久宮)
places.w: One of the Ryūkyū Hassha, founded in the Chenghua era (1465–87) and enshrining Izanami with Hayatamao and Kotosakao (the Kumano deities); annual festival on 15 May. Tucked into a hillside in Tomari.
places.k: Hillside Kumano shrine of the Ryūkyū Eight in Tomari

places.n: Gajanbira Park night view (がじゃんびら公園)
places.w: Hilltop park on the Oroku heights, the night-view spot closest to Naha Airport: a 500 m promenade looks across Naha port to the city lights. The name comes from Okinawan dialect, gajan (mosquito) + bira (slope).

places.n: Painagama Beach, Hirara (パイナガマビーチ)
places.w: The closest beach to downtown Hirara, walkable from the port; its name (南長間) means 'long southern beach' in Miyako dialect. A barrier-free city beach popular for sunset and an easy first swim on Miyako.
places.k: Miyako's walk-in town beach, minutes from Hirara

places.n: Ikema Wetlands, Ikema Island (池間湿原)
places.w: At 38 ha the largest wetland in Okinawa Prefecture, in the centre of Ikema Island; selected as one of Japan's 500 Important Wetlands, and since 1 Nov 2011 the whole island is a national wildlife (bird) protection area. An observation tower overlooks the marsh and its migratory birds.
places.k: Okinawa's largest wetland, a birding stop on Ikema

places.n: JUNGLIA Okinawa theme park, Nakijin/Nago (ジャングリア沖縄)
places.w: A 60-hectare nature theme park on a former golf course straddling Nakijin and Nago at the edge of Yanbaru, opened 25 July 2025 by Katana Inc. (led by ex-USJ marketer Tsuyoshi Morioka): animatronic-dinosaur rides, buggy safaris, bungee and an aerial course, plus a spa annex and 15 restaurants (Stars and Stripes; The Japan Times; nippon.com/Jiji).
places.k: Northern Okinawa's new jungle theme park (opened July 2025)

places.n: Yanbaru Kuina Ecological Exhibit 'Kuina no Mori', Kunigami (ヤンバルクイナ生態展示学習施設 クイナの森)
places.w: The place to actually see the Okinawa rail (Yanbaru kuina), the flightless national natural monument found only in Yanbaru: a live exhibit and learning facility in Ada village, part of the Ada Kuina Fureai Park. The OCVB features it in its ethical-travel series on learning about Yanbaru nature; Mapple lists it (9:00–17:00, last entry 16:30).
places.nat: ヤンバルクイナ生態展示学習施設 クイナの森

places.n: OKINAWA Fruits Land, Nago (OKINAWAフルーツらんど)
places.w: A tropical theme park in Nago on the road to Churaumi, where you walk among tropical and subtropical fruit trees and colourful southern birds and taste the fruit; listed by the OCVB and described on Japanese Wikipedia (open daily 10:00–17:30).
places.k: Tropical fruit trees and birds, then the tasting

places.n: Miyako Jinja — Japan's southernmost shrine, Hirara (宮古神社)
places.w: Founded in 1590 (Tenshō 18), Miyako Jinja is the southernmost Shinto shrine in Japan. It enshrines the three Kumano deities alongside three deified Miyako chieftains (tuyumya), including Nakasone Tuyumya; its annual festival falls on 26 October.
places.k: Japan's southernmost Shinto shrine, in central Hirara

places.n: Imgya Marine Garden, Gusukube (イムギャーマリンガーデン)
places.w: A city-run seaside park built around a natural, wave-sheltered inlet (Imgya / Ingya coast) on Miyako's south shore, set up to promote marine recreation and tourism; the calm water suits snorkelling and a walking trail climbs to a lookout over the cove.
places.k: Calm natural inlet for snorkelling on Miyako's south coast
places.nat: イムギャーマリンガーデン

places.n: Cape Nishi-hennazaki, Karimata (西平安名崎)
places.w: The cape at Miyako's north-western tip, facing the East China Sea, with a lookout over Ikema Ōhashi and Ikema Island. Its wind turbines were felled by typhoons in 2002–03 and three were rebuilt in 2008.
places.k: Wind-turbine cape with a panorama of Ikema Ōhashi

places.n: Kishimoto Shokudo (きしもと食堂)
places.ad: near Motobu Municipal Market, Motobu, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: Soba shop founded in 1905 near the Motobu market: flat noodles still made with tree-ash lye water, in a light bonito-and-soy broth with thick boneless rib, kamaboko and island onion.

places.n: King Tacos Kin (キングタコス 金武本店)
places.w: The taco-rice institution in downtown Kin: seasoned taco meat, cheese, lettuce and tomato over rice — the dish created in Kin in 1984 by Matsuzo Gibo of Parlor Senri.
places.nat: キングタコス 金武本店

places.n: RuLer's TACORiCE Ginowan Honten (ルーラーズタコライス 宜野湾本店)
places.w: A taco-rice specialist whose Ginowan flagship serves eight original recipes — classic cheese, BBQ, Caesar, teriyaki and the avocado-bacon-cheese ABC — in sizes up to extra-large, with about ten extra toppings. Tabirai lists it among Okinawa's nine top taco-rice shops.
places.nat: ルーラーズタコライス 宜野湾本店

places.n: Rotary Drive-In, Michi-no-Eki Kadena (ロータリードライブイン)
places.w: Opened in 1975 as a restaurant with a take-out window, on the site where Michi-no-Eki Kadena stands now. Its American-style menu was a rarity that won over locals and visitors. The founders' daughter took over in 2016; the dining room closed after the renovation and the pandemic, and it now runs as a take-out counter on the roadside station's ground floor, famous for its jumbo cheeseburger.
places.nat: ロータリードライブイン

places.n: Jimmy's Ōyama (ジミー 大山店)
places.w: The first shop of Jimmy's, the American-style bakery, deli and import grocery founded in 1956 and loved by Okinawans ever since. Its fresh-baked pies, apple pie above all, cream puffs and other pastries are the draw, alongside imported groceries, wine and awamori.

places.n: Stand Suehiro, Sakaemachi (スタンド末広)
places.ad: Ōyama Apartment 1F, 388-9 Asato, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: A small standing-style bar on the edge of Sakaemachi Market, named after the shokudō the owner's grandmother ran in Osaka. OTV's Sakaemachi bar-hop series calls its house-made otōshi the 'strongest' it found, and Smart Magazine singles out the meat pie as the popular order.

places.n: Okinawa Kushikatsu Senbero-ya, Sakaemachi (沖縄串カツ せんべろ家)
places.w: A red-lantern kushikatsu counter inside Sakaemachi Market, sister shop of the bone-broth specialist Honejiru-ya. It fries Osaka-style kushikatsu and runs a 'senbero' set (4 items for ¥1,000); beef kushikatsu is the best seller, and OTV's Sakaemachi bar-hop series also praises its chicken wings.
places.nat: 沖縄串カツ せんべろ家

places.n: BOULANGERIE BZ, Yogi (ブーランジェリービズ)
places.w: A neighbourhood counter bakery in Yogi where staff fetch the breads you name. Its glazed mini croissants, ¥50 each and sold by the bag, are the famous item and are often reserved a day ahead; RETRIP and the local site TAGOO both list it among Naha's favourite bakeries.
places.nat: ブーランジェリービズ

places.n: Ryōtei Naha, Tsuji (料亭那覇)
places.w: A ryōtei founded in 1949 in Tsuji, Naha's old entertainment quarter, now over 70 years old. Dinner is a set Ryūkyū or Japanese-Ryūkyū course served while professional dancers perform classical Ryūkyū dance. It holds the 'Ryūkyū ryōri ga ajiwaeru mise' certification and is listed by OCVB and Rurubu.

places.n: Yaeyama Ryōri Kotōzan Tantei, Shuri (八重山料理 虎頭山 潭亭)
places.w: A reservation-only Yaeyama-cuisine restaurant on Torazuyama hill in Shuri, looking out over Naha and Shuri Castle. Most ingredients come from Ishigaki, and the owner does every step of the cooking. It is a certified Ryūkyū-cuisine shop and is profiled by OCVB, Tabirai and Okinawa Traveler.
places.nat: 八重山料理 虎頭山 潭亭

places.n: Shuzen Maeda, Kume (酒膳 眞榮田)
places.w: A small Ryūkyū-cuisine dining bar in Kume holding the 'Ryūkyū ryōri ga ajiwaeru mise' certification. Okinawa Traveler's feature on the certified shops recommends its white-miso rafute, jīmāmi-dōfu and minudaru, a court-cuisine dish of pork steamed in a black-sesame crust.

places.n: Arakaki Chinsukō Honpo, Kokusai-dōri Makishi (新垣ちんすこう本舗 牧志店)
places.w: The Kokusai-dōri shop of the old Ryūkyū confectioner whose line goes back to Arakaki Shukiki, a royal-kitchen cook at Shuri Castle. Its founder is credited with turning chinsukō from a steamed cake into the baked biscuit sold today, and the shop still makes it by hand. Listed by OCVB, Mapple and Rurubu.
places.nat: 新垣ちんすこう本舗 牧志店

places.n: Matsubaraya Seika, Matsuo (松原屋製菓)
places.w: A family confectioner more than 70 years old off Kokusai-dōri, selling everyday Okinawan sweets: sātā andāgī, pōpō crepe rolls, mūchī and the celebratory nū-manjū. OTV's Okitive profiles it as a long-standing shop, and Rurubu lists it.

places.n: Takara Shokudō, Wakasa (高良食堂)
places.w: A neighbourhood shokudō in the residential streets behind Wakasa beach, serving Okinawan home cooking. Its champurū is seasoned with miso for a gentle taste, and the clear soup of pork bone and bonito is its most praised point. Listed by OCVB, Mapple and Rurubu.

places.n: Taishū Shokudō Ikariya, Maejima (大衆食堂 いかり屋)
places.ad: Okinawa Sailors Hall 1F, 3-25-50 Maejima, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: A big-menu harbour canteen on the ground floor of the seafarers' hall by Tomarin port, cooking champurū, Okinawa soba and Japanese, Western and Chinese plates. Okinawa Times' 'driver's meals' series covered its all-you-can-eat curry, and Ryukyu Shimpo and OTV both profile it as a lunch-and-dinner local favourite.
places.nat: 大衆食堂 いかり屋

places.n: Kiraku, Makishi Public Market 2F (きらく 第一牧志公設市場)
places.ad: 2F Naha City Daiichi Makishi Public Market, 2-10-1 Matsuo, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: One of the upstairs restaurants of the rebuilt Makishi Public Market that carries on the market's 'mochiage' custom. You buy up to three kinds of fish or meat from the stalls on the ground floor and Kiraku cooks them for a ¥500 fee, for example parrotfish as sashimi, in garlic butter or simmered in soy. Ryukyu Shimpo walked through the system with its manager, and co-trip's market guide covers the mochiage experience.
places.nat: きらく 第一牧志公設市場

places.n: Yonabaru-ya, Yonabaru (与那原家)
places.w: A Yonabaru soba house founded in 1985, serving homemade noodles in two broths — a light pork/chicken/bonito/kombu soup and a rich multi-bone one — with nankotsu-soki soba the most popular bowl. It was one of eight southern shops chosen in Okinawa Times' 2023 poll of 900 noodle lovers, and also ranks in an ITmedia Netorabo reader poll of Okinawa soba.

places.n: Inamine Hiyashimono Senmon Oshokujidokoro, Itoman (いなみね冷し物専門 お食事処)
places.w: A long-running Itoman cold-sweets and set-meal shop (31 years per OCVB's Itoman listing) famous for its shirokuma — a mound of kintoki shaved ice decorated as a bear's face — alongside Okinawa soba and champurū set meals. Ryukyu Shimpo's 'Uchinā Aji Māi' column profiled the shirokuma, a house speciality for about 30 years, and Rurubu lists it as a signature Itoman sweets stop.
places.nat: いなみね冷し物専門 お食事処

places.n: Umibudō Farm Umin-chi, Itoman (海ぶどう農園 海ん道)
places.w: A working sea-grape (umibudō) farm on the Itoman coast with a shop, its own Okinawa soba restaurant and picking experiences; its signature is soft serve folded with fresh-picked sea grapes. Ryukyu Shimpo reported on the farm and OCVB's official Itoman–Tomigusuku 'fishermen's-town gourmet' course includes it as a stop.
places.nat: 海ぶどう農園 海ん道

places.n: Do~me Gohan Café, Ryukyu Glass Village, Itoman (土～夢ごはんカフェ)
places.ad: 169 Fukuchi, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan (Ryukyu Glass Village)
places.w: The café beside the glass-blowing workshop at Ryukyu Glass Village, serving meat and fish mains — notably butter-soy gurukun, Okinawa's prefectural fish — with island-vegetable side dishes on local pottery and Ryukyu glass. JAL's Skyward crew picks recommend it and Stripes Okinawa reviewed it.

places.n: JA Farmers Market Itoman Umanchu Ichiba, Michi-no-Eki Itoman (ファーマーズマーケットいとまん うまんちゅ市場)
places.ad: Nishizaki-chō, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan (inside Michi-no-Eki Itoman)
places.w: Opened in November 2002 inside Michi-no-Eki Itoman, it is one of Okinawa's largest farm stands, with 1,000+ contracted growers and the highest footfall of the prefecture's ten JA farmers markets — Okinawa Times reported it passing 16 million visitors, and Ryukyu Shimpo covered its 10-millionth. OCVB's official Itoman gourmet course recommends its handmade onigiri, sweets and tropical fruit.
places.nat: ファーマーズマーケットいとまん うまんちゅ市場

places.n: Captain Kangaroo, Nago (キャプテンカンガルー)
places.w: A burger shop that began as an Osaka bar in 1999 and opened in Nago in 2007, moving to its current Umusa site in 2020. Stars and Stripes Okinawa calls it a hot spot for its taco rice as well as its burgers; OTV Okitive profiles its Mexican-loaded 'Captain Kangaroo taco rice', and Smart Magazine ranks it among Okinawa's top one or two burger shops.
places.nat: キャプテンカンガルー

places.n: Nago Fishing Port Fish Market & Diner (名護漁港水産物直販所)
places.w: A fish-sales hall with an attached diner inside Nago fishing port on Route 58, cooking fish auctioned that day at the port. Ryukyu Shimpo's 'Uchinā aji māi' column praised its seafood bowl of many fish, Okinawa Times' driver-lunch column went for the squid-ink soup and tempura, and the Nago tourism association lists it.
places.nat: 名護漁港水産物直販所

places.n: Ōgimi Shīkwāsā Park (大宜味シークヮーサーパーク)
places.w: Billed by the OCVB as Okinawa's first shīkwāsā theme park, in the citrus's home village of Ōgimi: a free-entry factory where you watch the pressing line, compare juices from each month's harvest and eat in a restaurant cooking with shīkwāsā powder. Ryukyu Shimpo covered its completion as a local-produce revitalisation project; the Yanbaru three-villages tourism portal lists it.
places.nat: 大宜味シークヮーサーパーク

places.n: GATE1, Kin (ゲート1)
places.w: A retro-American diner facing Camp Hansen's Gate 1 in Kin, the birthplace of taco rice; Kin town's tourism site lists its big cheese-and-vegetable taco rice, jumbo burger and fried chicken, and notes it takes US dollars as well as yen. Stars and Stripes Okinawa names Gate 1, with King Tacos, as a long-running taco-rice favourite in Kin.

places.n: Bookcafe Okinawa Rail, Kunigami (ブックカフェ オキナワレイル)
places.ad: 2040-107 Ōho-shagahara, Okuma, Kunigami-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: An off-grid concrete book café on the forest road toward Yonaha-dake inside Yanbaru National Park, named for the Yanbaru kuina (Okinawa rail), running on solar power and spring water with walls of books. Ryukyu Shimpo covered its opening as a forest reading retreat; OTV Okitive calls it worth the trip, and Tabirai recommends the New York cheesecake and house-roasted coffee.
places.nat: ブックカフェ オキナワレイル

places.n: Taira Shōten, Ishigaki (平良商店)
places.w: A Tonoshiro soba shop facing Manta Park that won the grand prix of the Yaeyama-soba division at the 3rd Yaeyama Soba Championship (2017). Tabirai describes it as a locals' favourite for its soft-cartilage sōki soba and spicy miso vegetable soba, made with a broth from island moromi-pork bones; the Okinawa Times reported FamilyMart selling a cup-noodle version supervised by the shop.

places.n: Oshokujidokoro Sumubari, Karimata (お食事処 すむばり)
places.w: A shokudō by the approach to Ikema Ōhashi that specialises in Miyako's little-known local octopus: its signature 'Sumubari soba' and an ink-black octopus soba use tako from the nearby fishing ports. Tabirai lists it among nine Miyako soba shops locals vouch for; Smart Magazine explains how the kitchen makes the octopus so tender.
places.nat: お食事処 すむばり

places.n: Kaimiru, Ikema Island (海美来)
places.w: A pink-fronted seafood shokudō at the Ikema Island end of Ikema Ōhashi, looking out over 'Ikema blue'. Its turban-shell sazae soba is found nowhere else, per Tabirai's list of nine Miyako soba shops locals vouch for; the Miyako island tourism association also lists its handmade purple-sweet-potato mochi.

places.n: Shima Tōfu Haru-obaa Shokudō, Miyako (島とうふ 春おばぁ食堂)
places.w: A shokudō built around a family island-tofu business of more than 60 years; its most popular dish is yushi-dōfu soba, Miyako soba crowned with soft freshly-set tofu. Tabirai includes it in its nine Miyako soba shops locals vouch for, and Mapple lists it among Miyako's top-ten Miyako soba lunches.
places.nat: 島とうふ 春おばぁ食堂

places.n: Gabusoka Shokudo Honten (我部祖河食堂 本店)
places.w: Founded in 1966 and billed as the birthplace of soki soba: the founder, then a butcher, simmered unsold spare ribs for hours and laid them on soba. House-made wavy noodles, punchy pork-bone broth.
places.nat: 我部祖河食堂 本店

places.n: Yanbaru Soba (山原そば)
places.ad: 70-1 Izumi, Motobu, Kunigami District, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: The queue-before-opening star of the Motobu 'soba road' (Route 84): a mellow bonito-and-pork broth unchanged for four decades, soki or three-layer pork on top; closes when the noodles run out.

places.n: Mexico, Chatan (タコス専門店 メキシコ)
places.w: Taco-only shop serving since 1977 — one of the island's most famous taco joints, crisp shells stuffed with seasoned beef in the style US servicemen brought to Okinawa.
places.nat: タコス専門店 メキシコ

places.n: Zuisen Distillery (瑞泉酒造)
places.w: Shuri awamori maker descended from the distillers who supplied the royal court; free tour of the stills and fermentation tanks, a look into the kusu ageing cellar and a tasting of Zuisen and Omoro.

places.n: Mikasa Matsuyama (三笠 松山店)
places.w: Round-the-clock homestyle shokudō near the Prefectural Office: gōyā champurū, spam and egg, and the house 'chanpon' — Okinawa's stir-fry-on-rice take — in a room that feels like grandma's kitchen.

places.n: Jack's Steak House (ジャッキーステーキハウス)
places.w: Opened in 1953 under the US occupation and still displaying its 'A-sign' — the US-military approval certificate; the benchmark of Okinawa's post-war steak culture, open till 1 a.m.
places.nat: ジャッキーステーキハウス

places.n: Yūnangi (ゆうなんぎい)
places.w: Family-run Okinawan restaurant on a side street off Kokusai-dōri, serving home cooking since 1970 under US administration — hard to get a seat, rated among the best Okinawan food in Naha.

places.n: Hamaya Soba (そば専門店 浜屋)
places.w: Soba specialist by the Sunabe seawall, a local and tourist favourite for its soft-boned cartilage soki in a clean, salt-seasoned broth.

places.n: Charlie's Tacos, Koza (チャーリー多幸寿)
places.w: Koza taco counter a short walk from Kadena's Gate 2 where locals, mainlanders and Americans have queued for more than 60 years — one of the A-sign-era base-town originals.

places.n: Kojasobaya (古謝そば屋)
places.w: Miyako soba shop founded in 1932 by the Koja noodle-making family, under a red-tile roof; lunchtime queues for Miyako soba, soki soba and curry soba.

places.n: Rakuen no Kajitsu, Kurima Island (楽園の果実)
places.w: Farm café on Kurima Island using its own tree-ripened mango (July–Aug) and dragon fruit (July–Oct) in parfaits and sweets, plus a Miyako-beef rice bowl.

places.n: Doug's Burger Miyakojima (ダグズ・バーガー)
places.w: Island burger joint using 100 % Miyako-island beef, plus a burger of local yellow-fin tuna — the Miyako take on Okinawa's American-era burger culture.

places.n: Hamabe no Chaya (浜辺の茶屋)
places.w: Founded in 1994 as Okinawa's first seaside café: a driftwood lodge on a shallow beach whose window counter sits right over the water at high tide.

places.n: Café Kurukuma (カフェくるくま)
places.w: Cliff-top Asian-herb restaurant café with a terrace and herb-garden promenade looking out over the Pacific.

places.n: Shuri Soba (首里そば)
places.w: Lunch-only Shuri shop carrying on the noodle technique of a vanished Shuri original: unbleached flour pressed and rested over two days, a single soba on the menu, queues from before opening and sold out early.

places.n: Ryūkyū Cuisine Mie (琉球料理 美榮)
places.w: Founded in 1958 to reproduce the Ryūkyū royal court cuisine of Shō Junnan, gourmet son of the last king, in a wooden two-storey ryōtei behind a formal gate in Kumoji.

places.n: Izumi Soba (伊豆味そば)
places.ad: Izumi, Motobu, Kunigami District, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: Soba stop on the Route 84 'soba road' through Izumi, picked in Okinawa Times' 2023 poll of 900 noodle lovers as one of the north's best.

places.n: Shinzan Soba (新山そば)
places.w: Nago soba house founded in 1925 and run by the third generation: thick, springy flat noodles in an agu-pork-bone and bonito broth; profiled by the Okinawa Times as a century-old favourite.

places.n: Tamakaya Soba Honten (そば処 玉家 本店)
places.w: Soba specialist prized for the balance of broth, noodles and toppings — first on the Okinawa Times 2023 reader poll's southern list.
places.nat: そば処 玉家 本店

places.n: Suunumee (すーぬめぇ)
places.w: Soba in an old Okinawan house in Kokuba; the 'special' piles on soki, belly and the owner's prized tebichi. On the Okinawa Times 2023 reader-poll list.

places.n: Nemu Isa (根夢 伊佐店)
places.w: Ginowan soba shop whose broth blends separately made bonito and pork-bone stocks at seven to three; picked in the Okinawa Times 2023 reader poll's central list.

places.n: Misato Soba (美里そば)
places.w: Okinawa City soba specialist with a layered chicken, pork-bone and bonito broth; on both the Okinawa Times 2023 central poll list and KozaWeb's city top ten.

places.n: Komehachi Soba (米八そば)
places.w: Awase soba shop known for its 'triathlon' bowl topped with all three Okinawan pork cuts; on the Okinawa Times 2023 central list and KozaWeb's top ten.

places.n: Kinatsuyu (八重山そば処 来夏世)
places.w: Old-house Yaeyama-soba specialist in Ishigaki town keeping the simple, light traditional flavour; the soba set with jūshī rice draws a noon queue. 'The royal road of Yaeyama soba' in the Okinawa Times 2023 reader poll.
places.nat: 八重山そば処 来夏世

places.n: Sennichi (千日)
