places.w: Naha's classic zenzai parlour near Naminoue Shrine, in business since the 1950s (the founders' Yafune Shokudo, then 'Sennichi' in Kume from 1962). Order the Okinawa zenzai: plump, slow-stewed beans under a triangle of hand-shaved ice.

places.n: A&W Makiminato (A&W 牧港店)
places.w: A&W came to Okinawa in 1963, years before mainland Japan — the 24-hour Makiminato drive-in on Route 58 is the chain's Okinawa flagship. Root beer in a frosted mug, curly fries and a burger is a rite of passage.

places.n: Steakhouse 88 Tsuji Honten (ステーキハウス88 辻本店)
places.w: Flagship of the Steakhouse 88 chain, descended from 'CLUB88', an A-sign restaurant licensed for US personnel in 1955. Neon diner room, 20-plus steak cuts, open till 1 am — the classic Okinawan 'shime' (end-of-night) steak.
places.nat: ステーキハウス88 辻本店

places.n: Nakamura Soba (なかむらそば)
places.w: Roadside soba house near Manza Beach: preservative-free house noodles, a light but bonito-rich broth and pork belly that falls apart at a touch; the aasa soba works sea lettuce into both noodles and topping.

places.n: OKINAWA SOBA EIBUN
places.w: A newer-generation Naha soba shop that made both the Okinawa Times 900-reader noodle poll and Okinawa Traveler's five soba shops locals recommend with confidence.

places.n: Yagiya (屋宜家)
places.ad: 1172 Ōgan, Yaese, Shimajiri District, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: Soba served in a registered cultural-property red-tiled house; choose classic, soy-milk or seaweed noodles in a light but deep bonito broth.

places.n: Ufuya (百年古家 大家)
places.w: A century-old Okinawan farmhouse compound in the hills above Nago serving soki soba and agu pork; one of Okinawa Traveler's locals-recommend five and on Stars and Stripes' soba trail.

places.n: Arakaki Zenzai-ya (新垣ぜんざい屋)
places.w: Motobu's half-century-old zenzai shop that does exactly one thing: sweet stewed red kidney beans buried under a peak of shaved ice, bought with a ticket from the door.

places.n: Inaka Ryōri no Mise Kura, Miyako (田舎料理の店 蔵)
places.w: Country-cooking izakaya in Hirara using island miso in champuru and rafute; prefecture-certified for Ryukyu cuisine and a Mapple guidebook pick.

places.n: Urizun (古酒と琉球料理 うりずん)
places.w: Opened 15 August 1972 by gathering bottles from every awamori distillery in Okinawa — the bar that brought awamori back to the people. Order duru-ten, the fried taro croquette Okinawa Times traces to this kitchen, and a flight of kūsu (aged awamori).
places.nat: 古酒と琉球料理 うりずん

places.n: Irabu Soba Kame (伊良部そば かめ)
places.w: Irabu Island's soba stop, where the bonito hits you first; reached over the Irabu Bridge and named in both Okinawa Times' Miyako soba coverage and Mapple's Miyako-soba top ten.

places.n: Maruyoshi Shokudō (丸吉食堂)
places.w: Out in Gusukube, a family shokudō serving the owner's mother's Miyako soba: pork-bone broth perfumed with garlic and big soki ribs.

places.n: Yamato Shokudō (大和食堂)
places.w: Hirara regulars' shop serving the same plain, honest Miyako soba for some forty years.

places.n: Minato Shokudō, Miyako (みなと食堂)
places.w: Harbour-side shokudō near Sunayama whose house noodles are kneaded with aosa seaweed and served in a broth from bonito trimmings — a taste found only here.

places.n: Jinku-ya (じんく屋)
places.w: Counter run by Kusamatsu Seimen, one of Miyako's two big noodle makers: chewy fresh noodles, simple bonito soup.

places.n: Ishigaki-gyū Sumibi Yakiniku Yamamoto (石垣牛 炭火焼肉 やまもと)
places.w: The Ishigaki-beef yakiniku house locals queue for: buying whole animals means rare cuts on the board, grilled over charcoal; opens at 17:00 and closes when the meat runs out.
places.nat: 石垣牛 炭火焼肉 やまもと

places.n: Kimi Shokudō, Ishigaki (キミ食堂)
places.w: Ishigaki town shokudō famous for its miso-broth take on Yaeyama soba — a noodle-lovers' poll pick and one of Rurubu's 'creative' soba bowls.

places.n: Dachibin Naha Kumoji (沖縄居酒屋 抱瓶 那覇久茂地店)
places.w: The Naha outpost of an Okinawan izakaya that made its name in Tokyo, in a Shōwa-era wooden house; prefecture-certified for Ryukyu cuisine.
places.nat: 沖縄居酒屋 抱瓶 那覇久茂地店

places.n: Orion Happy Park — Orion Beer Nago Brewery (オリオンハッピーパーク)
places.w: Okinawa's own beer since 1957: the Nago plant's tour ends with a tasting of just-brewed Orion Draft; shop, restaurant and a small history gallery.
places.nat: オリオンハッピーパーク

places.n: Chatan Harbor Brewery & Restaurant (チャタンハーバーブルワリー)
places.w: Seafront brewpub a few minutes from American Village brewing five year-round beers on site, with a terrace over the East China Sea at sunset.
places.nat: チャタンハーバーブルワリー

places.n: Helios Distillery (ヘリオス酒造)
places.w: Founded as a rum distiller in 1961 and brewing Okinawa's pioneering craft beer since 1996; the free tour shows 2,600 barrels of aging awamori stacked to the roof.

places.n: Ganso Nakamoto Tempura, Ōjima (元祖中本てんぷら店)
places.w: The queue-every-day tempura stand facing Ōjima fishing port, attached to a fish shop: thick-battered Okinawan tempura of fish, squid, mozuku seaweed and vegetables, eaten hot by the sea.

places.n: Nantō Shokurakuen, Kume Island (南島食楽園)
places.w: Big open izakaya by Eef Beach built around Kume's own produce: kuruma prawns raised in deep-ocean water, sea grapes, island red chicken, grouper and octopus, from Okinawan plates to nigiri.

places.n: Sukeroku Kamaboko, Kume Island (助ろく)
places.w: Kume's fish-cake maker, carrying on a 60-year-old craft: chewy island kamaboko flavoured with kuruma prawn, mozuku or squid ink — a classic island snack.

places.n: Sobadokoro Takenoko, Taketomi (そば処 竹の子)
places.ad: Taketomi Village, Taketomi Island, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: Taketomi's most popular eating house, around forty years old, ladling the previous generation's Yaeyama soba in the red-tile village.

places.n: Tamagusuku Coffee Roasters (タマグスクコーヒー)
places.w: Ten-seat roaster-café off Kokusai-dōri often called the island's best cup: the owner asks what you like, then drips light-to-dark single origins one cup at a time.

places.n: Coffee Yatai Hibari-ya (珈琲屋台 ひばり屋)
places.w: An open-air coffee stall tucked into a leafy back alley near Makishi Station — ground-to-order hand drip and a famous deep-roast iced coffee on mismatched chairs.
places.nat: 珈琲屋台 ひばり屋

places.n: rokkan COFFEE SHURI (ロッカン コーヒー シュリ)
places.w: Second shop (Oct 2023) of Naha roaster rokkan COFFEE CREATORS, opening at 6 am near Shuri Castle — a 'sixth sense' coffee before the castle crowds.
places.nat: ロッカン コーヒー シュリ

places.n: Tacos Café Tacoloco, Chatan (タコスカフェ タコロコ)
places.w: American Village taquería making properly Mexican tacos — spices shipped from Mexico — a counterpoint to Okinawa's crunchy-shell post-war tacos.
places.nat: タコスカフェ タコロコ

places.n: Itoman Fishermen's Co-op Osakana Center, Michi-no-Eki Itoman (糸満漁協 お魚センター)
places.w: Eleven fishmongers run by the Itoman fishermen's co-op inside Japan's southernmost roadside station: choose fish for a kaisendon, nigiri, fish soup or Okinawan tempura and eat on the spot, 10:00–19:00.
places.nat: 糸満漁協 お魚センター

places.n: Mendokoro Tiandaa (麺処 てぃあんだー)
places.w: Cult Naha soba shop known for house-made noodles; the fūchibā soba arrives fragrant with Okinawan mugwort. In both Okinawa Traveler's soba feature and Mapple's Okinawa-soba round-up.
places.nat: 麺処 てぃあんだー

places.n: Sobaya Yoshiko, Motobu (そば屋よしこ)
places.w: One of the stars of Motobu's 'soba highway' (Prefectural Route 84, 20-plus soba shops): come for the meltingly braised tebichi on a pork-bonito-kombu broth.

places.n: Teppanyaki Steak House Shiki, Sonoda Honten (ステーキハウス四季 園田本店)
places.w: A Koza teppanyaki steak house running for close to half a century in the post-war steak heartland by Kadena; chefs sear the steak on the iron in front of you.
places.nat: ステーキハウス四季 園田本店

places.n: Highway Drive-In Restaurant, Okinawa City (ハイウェイ食堂)
places.w: Opened in 1972 by a US Army cook as an A-sign establishment and seemingly frozen in time since: huge diner plates, low prices, fast service, open till 2 am on Route 75.

places.n: Blue Seal Makiminato Honten (ブルーシール 牧港本店)
places.w: 'Born in America, raised in Okinawa': Blue Seal started in 1948 supplying the US bases and moved to this Makiminato drive-in in 1963. The flagship was rebuilt and reopened in 2024 to a 400-person queue — order beni-imo or salt-chinsukō.
places.nat: ブルーシール 牧港本店

places.n: Onna no Eki Nakayukui Ichiba (おんなの駅 なかゆくい市場)
places.w: West-coast roadside market that every drive north stops at: island produce, snack stalls frying sata andagi (brown sugar, beni-imo and more), and Ryu-pin's mountainous tropical-fruit kakigōri.
places.nat: おんなの駅 なかゆくい市場

places.n: Michi-no-Eki Kyoda — Yanbaru Bussan Center (道の駅許田)
places.w: The roadside station at the end of the Okinawa Expressway, gateway to Yanbaru: produce from the twelve northern towns and a takeout row famous for hot Okinawan tempura and tacos. Renewed in 2021.

places.n: Awamori to Okinawa Ryōri Gōya, Miyako (泡盛と沖縄料理 郷家)
places.w: Hirara's classic shimauta izakaya: Miyako's own awamori brands, island home cooking, and nightly sanshin folk-song sets that end with the whole room dancing kachāshī.
places.nat: 泡盛と沖縄料理 郷家

places.n: RICCO gelato, Miyako (リッコジェラート)
places.w: Italian-trained gelato maker in Hirara churning Miyako's own mangoes, fruits and even island salt and vegetables into some thirty flavours.

places.n: Shima Café Tunkaraya, Miyako (島cafe とぅんからや)
places.w: Hilltop café in southern Miyako looking over the sea, cooking 'made in Miyako' lunches and fruit-heavy desserts.

places.n: Ishigaki-jima Milmil Honpo (石垣島ミルミル本舗)
places.w: Dairy-farm gelato stand on a hill above the sea west of Ishigaki town; the plain milk flavour is the best seller. Open until sunset.

places.n: Benriya Yulinglong, Sakaemachi (べんり屋 玉玲瓏)
places.w: The pioneer of Sakaemachi market's night drinking: when the stalls shutter, tables fill the alley for its hand-made gyōza. Both Rurubu and Mapple name it first among the market's after-dark haunts.

places.n: Nakamura-ya, Kumoji (海産物料理とあわもりの店 なかむら家)
places.w: Seafood-and-awamori izakaya in Kumoji where regulars come for whatever the boats brought in — island fish sashimi and simmered fish, washed down with awamori.
places.nat: 海産物料理とあわもりの店 なかむら家

places.n: Karakara to Chibugwā (カラカラとちぶぐゎ〜)
places.ad: Yamako 2nd Bldg 1F, 3-15-15 Kumoji, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: Naha's awamori-specialist bar: bottles from every distillery in the prefecture and aged kūsu past thirty years, with three awamori sommeliers to steer you; prefecture-certified for Ryukyu cuisine.

places.n: Kozakura (小桜)
places.w: A seventy-year-old koryōriya off Kokusai-dōri, believed to be the oldest surviving restaurant of its era in Naha; the third-generation owner keeps both old and new Okinawan dishes on the menu.

places.n: oHacorté Minatogawa Honten (オハコルテ 港川本店)
places.w: The fruit-tart shop (founded 2009) that made Minatogawa's 'Stateside Town' — some thirty shops and cafés in converted 1950s US military housing — a destination; glossy seasonal tarts in a little white house.
places.nat: オハコルテ 港川本店

places.n: Pizza Kissa Kajinhō, Motobu (ピザ喫茶 花人逢)
places.w: Red-tiled old-house café on a hilltop above Motobu serving the same home-made pizza for a quarter-century; on clear days Ie-jima, Sesoko and Minna float on the horizon.

places.n: Yachimun Kissa Shīsā-en, Motobu (やちむん喫茶 シーサー園)
places.w: A red-roofed Okinawan farmhouse swallowed by subtropical forest, with more than a hundred local potters' shīsā lions perched on roofs and walls around the tables.
places.nat: やちむん喫茶 シーサー園

places.n: Cafe ichara, Motobu (カフェ イチャラ)
places.w: A Motobu forest café picked by Rurubu, Mapple and Okinawa Traveler's 'sea or forest?' round-up of northern cafés.

places.n: Shima Ryōri Izakaya Adan-tei, Ishigaki (島料理居酒屋 あだん亭)
places.w: Ishigaki town izakaya cooking genuinely Yaeyaman dishes from island produce — try the champuru of adan (screw-pine) shoots — and the only Yaeyama restaurant on the prefecture's Ryukyu-cuisine certified list.
places.nat: 島料理居酒屋 あだん亭

places.n: Michi-no-Eki Yuiyui Kunigami (道の駅 ゆいゆい国頭)
places.w: The Yanbaru roadside station that gathers Kunigami village's food: Oku-grown green tea, karagi tea and the local Kunigami doughnuts — the last big food stop before Cape Hedo.
places.nat: 道の駅 ゆいゆい国頭

places.n: Michi-no-Eki Toyosaki (道の駅 豊崎)
places.w: The roadside station closest to Naha Airport, stocked with Tomigusuku's mango products and island produce — a last-stop for food souvenirs.

places.n: Takaesu Soba, Urasoe (高江洲そば)
places.w: An Urasoe institution counted among the 'traditional royal-road' soba shops by Rurubu and voted into the Okinawa Times noodle-lovers' central-region list.

places.n: Kingetsu Soba Yomitan Honten (金月そば 読谷本店)
places.w: Yomitan soba house on both Okinawa Traveler's area-by-area soba list and Rurubu's 16 best Okinawa-soba shops.
places.nat: 金月そば 読谷本店

places.n: Chadokoro Makabe Chinā, Itoman (茶処 真壁ちなー)
places.w: Soba and herb tea served in a red-tiled, stone-walled homestead whose house and grounds are a national Registered Tangible Cultural Property — the old southern-village Okinawa landscape intact.

places.n: Keishoku no Mise Ruby, Tomari (軽食の店ルビー)
places.w: Sixty-plus-year-old Tomari diner whose name belies mountainous portions: some 80 dishes from champuru to loco moco, but half the room orders the C-lunch. Namie Amuro used to drop in after dance practice.

places.n: Kaiyō Shokudō, Tomigusuku (海洋食堂)
places.w: Tomigusuku shokudō famous for yushi-dōfu, soft just-made island tofu carried over from the adjoining tofu works and served in soup or soba.

places.n: Mori no Kenja, Ishigaki (森の賢者)
places.w: Small Ishigaki-town kitchen cooking island vegetables, fish and Ishigaki beef without chemical seasonings, with awamori, sake and more than 45 home-made fruit and herb liqueurs; book ahead.

places.n: Maguro Senmon Izakaya Hitoshi, Ishigantō (まぐろ専門居酒屋 ひとし 石敢當店)
places.w: Ishigaki's famous tuna izakaya, packed with locals and visitors alike for heaped plates of just-landed island tuna; book or queue at 16:30.
places.nat: まぐろ専門居酒屋 ひとし 石敢當店

places.n: KITCHEN inaba, Iriomote (キッチン イナバ)
places.ad: 742-6 Uehara, Taketomi, Yaeyama District, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: Iriomote's island-food kitchen near Uehara port: rare local ingredients — irabu sea-snake soup, gazami crab, Ryukyu wild boar in season — alongside traditional and Western-style plates, with jungle-green mountains in the windows.

places.n: Shima Gourmet ROCO, Iriomote (島ぐるめ ROCO)
places.ad: 58 Uehara, Taketomi, Yaeyama District, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: Uehara dining room cooking Iriomote's sea and mountain catch — grilled crab, sashimi salad, squid-ink rice croquettes and grouper simmered in island salt.

places.n: Umi-no-Eki Ayahashi-kan, Kaichū-dōro (海の駅 あやはし館)
places.w: The 'sea station' halfway along the 5 km Kaichū-dōro causeway: local produce and the Kaichū Chaya restaurant upstairs serving soki soba and taco rice over the shallows.
places.nat: 海の駅 あやはし館

places.n: Nuchi Māsu Salt Factory, Miyagi Island (ぬちまーす観光製塩ファクトリー)
places.w: Clifftop salt works across the Kaichū-dōro on Miyagi Island, where a patented spray-drying method snows mineral-rich salt inside the factory; free 10-minute tours every 20 minutes, a sea-view restaurant and shop.
places.nat: ぬちまーす観光製塩ファクトリー

places.n: Awamori Masahiro Gallery, Itoman (泡盛まさひろギャラリー)
places.w: Gallery-shop of Masahiro Distillery (founded 1883): watch the production line through glass, browse displays on awamori's history and taste for free.
places.nat: 泡盛まさひろギャラリー

places.n: Uema Kashiten Factory — Suppaiman (上間菓子店 工場見学)
places.w: Free factory tour of the maker of Suppaiman, Okinawa's cult dried-plum snack and its mascot; watch the plums and candies being made (video only on Saturdays).
places.nat: 上間菓子店 工場見学

places.n: Restaurant Marumi-ya, Zamami (レストラン まるみ屋)
places.ad: Zamami village, Zamami Island, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: Five minutes from Zamami port: hearty daily set lunches built on island produce — mozuku seaweed champuru and house-made jīmāmi peanut tofu are the favourites.
places.nat: レストラン まるみ屋

places.n: Hanagasa Shokudō (花笠食堂)
places.w: A popular old-style shokudō off the Heiwa-dōri arcade serving Okinawan home cooking as set meals: pick white, brown or red (sekihan) rice and one of five soups including inamuruchi and nakami-jiru. Its sweet house iced tea is famous enough to have been sold in cartons.

places.n: Uchinā Chaya Buku-Buku, Tsuboya (うちなー茶屋 ぶくぶく)
places.w: A small teahouse on Tsuboya's pottery street that whips bukubuku-cha, the frothy rice-and-jasmine tea with Ryūkyū-dynasty roots, in front of you. Named in Visit Okinawa's Naha guide.
places.nat: うちなー茶屋 ぶくぶく

places.n: Yagi Ryōri Misaki, Sakaemachi (山羊料理 美咲)
places.w: A goat-meat specialist in the Sakaemachi Market alleys — goat is a traditional Okinawan celebration food. Featured by both Stars and Stripes' Sakaemachi guide and Mapple's Sakaemachi restaurant roundup.

places.n: C&C BREAKFAST OKINAWA (シーアンドシー ブレックファスト オキナワ)
places.w: A breakfast café a minute off Kokusai-dōri built around 'a delicious breakfast while traveling' — açaí bowls, pancakes and eggs Benedict. Ryukyu Shimpo highlighted its sweet-salty bacon-and-waffle combination.
places.nat: シーアンドシー ブレックファスト オキナワ

places.n: Itoman Gyomin Shokudō (糸満漁民食堂)
places.w: Fish restaurant in the fishing town of Itoman, opened in 2013 in a building of stacked Ryūkyū limestone that won a Good Design Award and JCD Design Award. Its signature is the day's local fish butter-grilled until crisp outside and tender within.

places.n: Seifuku Shuzō awamori distillery, Ishigaki (請福酒造)
places.w: Ishigaki awamori maker founded in 1949, with a direct shop where the whole Seifuku range can be tasted and free ~15-minute factory tours at set times, no booking needed.

places.n: Yaesen Shuzō awamori distillery, Ishigaki (八重泉酒造)
places.w: Founded in 1955; the factory shop shows a 15-minute film of the distilling process and runs a tasting counter with shop-only bottles. Three Yaesen awamori won awards at a UK spirits competition (Ryukyu Shimpo).

places.n: Takamine Shuzōsho awamori distillery, Kabira (高嶺酒造所)
places.w: Small distillery beside Kabira Park making 'Omoto' awamori by hand — one of the few still using direct-fire (jika-bi) distillation; the process is visible through glass and tastings are offered.

places.n: Yakiniku Takesan-tei, Ishigaki (焼肉 たけさん亭)
places.w: Ishigaki-beef yakiniku whose owner holds cattle-auction buying rights and buys whole A4–A5 animals, so rarer cuts appear on the menu. Dinner only (closed Tue).

places.n: Yakiniku Kingyū, Ishigaki (焼肉 金牛)
places.w: Run by an Ishigaki family that has raised wagyu on the island for over 120 years; serves only its own Ishigaki beef, raised ~30 months and aged. Dinner only (closed Thu).

places.n: Yukishio Museum, Miyako (雪塩ミュージアム)
places.w: Showroom of the 'Yukishio' salt works, which makes powder-fine salt from limestone-filtered underground seawater; free guided looks at the production line, and the shop's Yukishio soft-serve is the draw.

places.n: Maeda Shokudō, Ōgimi (前田食堂)
places.w: Yanbaru noodle shop founded in 1972, on the way to Hiji Falls and Mt Yonaha; its signature gyūniku soba piles pepper-fried beef and bean sprouts on thin noodles, and weekend queues are the norm. Closes when the broth runs out.

places.n: Shima-buta Shichirin-yaki Manmi, Nago (島豚七輪焼 満味)
places.w: Reservation-essential grill house for Yanbaru island pork descended from agu: cuts and offal grilled over individual charcoal shichirin, with rare pork tongue and a horumon fried rice to finish. Dinner only (closed Sun–Mon).

places.n: Okinawa Ryōri Maruoki Shōten, Nago (沖縄料理 丸沖商店)
places.w: Nago restaurant certified under Okinawa Prefecture's 'shop where you can taste Ryūkyū cuisine' scheme; known for its agu-pork shabu-shabu course.
places.nat: 沖縄料理 丸沖商店

places.n: KOURI SHRIMP, Kouri Island (古宇利島 KOURI SHRIMP)
places.w: Kouri Island's garlic-shrimp stand serving Hawaiian-style shrimp plates; Stars and Stripes notes it has opened a new shop on the island.

places.n: Pork Tamago Onigiri Honten, Makishi (ポークたまごおにぎり本店)
places.w: The flagship of the 'Pōtama' shop that turned Okinawa's pork-and-egg onigiri into a takeaway icon; each one is pressed to order so the rice is hot and the egg fluffy. Opens early (7:00) for breakfast, closed Wednesdays.
places.nat: ポークたまごおにぎり本店

places.n: Fujiya Tomari Honten (富士家 泊本店)
places.w: The name many Okinawans give first for zenzai: fluffy shaved ice frozen from the bean-cooking syrup so it never dilutes, heaped over sweet kintoki beans. Open daily, later hours in summer.

places.n: Tomari Iyumachi Fish Market (泊いゆまち)
places.w: The Okinawa fisheries co-op's market by Tomari Port, where about 70 percent of the catch sold is tuna, delivered unfrozen the day it is landed. Stalls sell sashimi, seafood bowls, shellfish and mozuku to eat on the upstairs terrace.

places.n: Kokusai-dōri Yatai-mura (国際通り屋台村)
places.w: A food-stall village opened in 2015 just off Kokusai-dōri, with more than 20 counter stalls cooking Okinawan and island dishes from local ingredients — gurukun and parrotfish sushi, Agu pork dumplings, Ishigaki beef — from 11:00. A central stage hosts island songs and dances.

places.n: Arakaki Kashiten, Shuri Samukawa (新垣菓子店 首里寒川店)
places.w: A confectioner founded in 1932 by descendants of a cook to the Ryūkyū royal court, making chinsukō and other traditional Ryūkyū sweets at its Shuri shop.
places.nat: 新垣菓子店 首里寒川店

places.n: Ryūkyū Ryōri Nuchigafū (琉球料理 ぬちがふぅ)
places.ad: Tsuboya, Naha, Okinawa (hilltop off the southern end of Tsuboya Yachimun-dōri)
places.w: An elegant hilltop restaurant above the southern end of Tsuboya pottery street that Lonely Planet singles out for a memorable dinner of Ryūkyū cuisine. It is on Okinawa Prefecture's certified list of restaurants serving authentic Ryūkyū cuisine.
places.nat: 琉球料理 ぬちがふぅ

places.n: Mihama Shokudō, Chatan (みはま食堂)
places.w: Local shokudō by Chatan's Mihama known for hone-jiru — pork backbones and tofu simmered in a kombu broth and eaten by hand — and hone-soba heaped with bone-in sōki; both often sell out early.

places.n: Sanchōme no Shima Soba-ya, Ginowan (3丁目の島そば屋)
places.ad: 3-10-1 Kakazu, Ginowan, Okinawa, Japan (White Papillon Sato 101)
places.w: Newer Ginowan soba shop picked among the eight best soba shops of central Okinawa in Okinawa Times' 2023 poll of 900 noodle lovers; Okinawa TV's Okitive praised its noodles, soup and toppings, notably the uneven mix of three noodle cuts.

places.n: Tacos-ya Chatan (タコス屋 北谷店)
places.ad: 1-5 Miyagi, Chatan, Okinawa, Japan (near the Sunabe Seawall)
places.w: Small taco shop on a backstreet near the Sunabe Seawall that has fed locals and visitors for about 35 years; it still fries its house-made shells to order for a chewy-crisp texture, and its Tacos-ya Plate piles tacos, taco rice, onion rings and fries on one plate.

places.n: Emi no Mise, Ōgimi (笑味の店)
places.w: Opened in 1990 by Kinjō Shōko to pass on the food culture of Ōgimi, the 'longevity village'; a farm restaurant whose reservation-only chōju-zen longevity set is built on seasonal island vegetables she grows herself. Her book of Yanbaru grandmothers' kitchen wisdom was published in 2023 (Ryukyu Shimpo).

places.n: Okashi Goten Onna (御菓子御殿 恩納店)
places.ad: Onna-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan (coastal Route 58; red-gated palace-style shop)
places.w: The red-gated seaside flagship of the confectioner behind the 'original' beni-imo tart, made from 100% Okinawan purple sweet potato from contracted farmers with no preservatives or colouring; the baking line is visible through glass and a reservation-only tart-making class runs here.
places.nat: 御菓子御殿 恩納店

places.n: Mozuku Soba Kunnatu, Nanjō (もずくそばの店 くんなとぅ)
places.w: Facing Ōjima, a mozuku-farming centre, this shop kneads JAS-organic mozuku into its own soba noodles and serves them in a light bonito broth with tempura fried to order.
places.nat: もずくそばの店 くんなとぅ

places.n: Seaside Drive-In, Onna (シーサイドドライブイン)
places.ad: Nakadomari, Onna-son, Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan (Route 58, seaside)
places.w: Opened in 1967 under US administration and kept in its original style, neon signs and all; the signature creamy pork-bone soup is a take-out ritual for west-coast beach days, and a 24-hour take-out counter sells burgers, shaved ice and sides.
places.nat: シーサイドドライブイン

places.n: Sakimoto Shuzōsho — hanazake distillery, Yonaguni (崎元酒造所)
places.w: Yonaguni's oldest distillery, still firing a traditional direct-fire pot still by hand; maker of the awamori 'Yonaguni' and of hanazake, the 60% first-run spirit that only Yonaguni is permitted to make. Distillery shop sells brewery-only bottles.

places.n: Pengin Shokudō, Ishigaki (辺銀食堂)
places.ad: Ishigaki city centre (7 min walk from Ishigaki bus terminal), Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: Birthplace of Ishigaki-jima rāyu, the hand-made island-salt-and-chilli oil that started Japan's 'edible rāyu' boom; at lunch the house order is jājan-suba (thick noodles with spicy miso), served until sold out.

places.n: Akashi Shokudō, Ishigaki (明石食堂)
places.ad: 360 Ihara, Ishigaki, Okinawa, Japan (Akashi area, north Ishigaki)
places.w: Old-guard north-Ishigaki shokudō about 40 minutes' drive from town, with queues before opening for its soft-bone sōki Yaeyama soba — clean pork-bone broth over round straight noodles. Ranked No.1 in a 2019 Okinawa-soba ranking reported by Ryukyu Shimpo.

places.n: Sakana-dokoro Shiken-bara, Miyako (肴処 志堅原)
places.w: Constantly-full izakaya on Hirara's Nishizato-dōri izakaya strip, serving fresh fish from the waters around Miyako as sashimi and salt-simmered mās-ni, with island awamori.

places.n: Kumejima Soba-dokoro Yan-kō, Kume Island (久米島そば処 やん小～)
places.w: Soba shop in an old Ryūkyū-style house making hand-cut noodles with Kume's deep-sea water; the signature is a rare miso-flavoured soba piled with island-grown bean sprouts. Lunch only (11:30-13:30), closed Sundays.
places.nat: 久米島そば処 やん小～

places.n: Yonejima Shuzō awamori distillery, Kume Island (米島酒造)
places.w: Small Kume Island distillery founded by Tabata Ryōtoku, who was drawn by the island's abundant water and varied geology; shop open 10-12 and 14-17, closed Sundays.

places.n: Fruit Parlour Kōrakuen, Ishigaki (光楽園)
places.w: Fruit parlour popular with both locals and visitors on Ishigaki, with a long line-up of chilled sweets built on tropical island fruit; featured in its own Rurubu piece and in Mapple's Ishigaki sweets round-up.

places.n: How Tree Gelato, Ishigaki (ハウトゥリージェラート)
places.w: Specialist in cold-plate marble ice cream mixing fresh fruit from the owners' own farm with Ishigaki Island milk; seasonal (Feb-Nov).
places.nat: ハウトゥリージェラート

places.n: Blue Turtle, Irabu Island (ブルー タートル)
places.ad: Irabu, Miyakojima, Okinawa, Japan (facing Toguchi-no-hama beach)
places.w: White sea-view café-restaurant on Irabu Island right in front of Toguchi-no-hama, one of Irabu's finest beaches; known for hamburg steak and for ice cream served over hidden layers of coloured shaved ice.

places.n: Shinzato Distillery (新里酒造)
places.ad: 12-17 Suzaki, Uruma, Okinawa 904-2234, Japan (head office 3-22-8 Koja, Okinawa City)
places.w: Founded in 1846, Shinzato is one of the oldest operating awamori distilleries in Okinawa, now run by the seventh-generation owner. It offers a roughly 45-minute factory tour combining traditional craft and modern technology, and has won the awamori grand prize at the All Japan sake competition.

places.n: Gordie's, Sunabe (ゴーディーズ)
places.w: Stand By Me-themed burger joint in a converted former on-base house near the Sunabe Seawall, serving coarse-ground, filler-free charcoal-grilled patties since 2007. Its Special Burger stacks two patties, thick bacon, a fried egg and cheese.

places.n: Pizza House Honten, Urasoe (ピザハウス 本店)
places.w: Founded in 1958 (its founders served Okinawa's first pizza), this American-style restaurant near Minatogawa Stateside Town is known for its roast beef and steaks. The main branch reopened in a 1950s-diner-style renovation on 15 March 2026 with the stated aim of becoming a '100-year restaurant'.

places.n: Miyanchi STUDIO & COFFEE, Okinawa City (みやんち STUDIO&COFFEE)
places.w: Red-tiled café and studio opened in 2012 in the hills of Okinawa City, produced by THE BOOM singer Kazufumi Miyazawa to share Okinawan folk music and food. Its signature is kara-soba, a soup-less Okinawa soba Miyazawa devised after eating a version on Ishigaki.

places.n: Tsurukame-dō Zenzai, Yomitan (鶴亀堂ぜんざい)
places.w: Zenzai shop near Zakimi Castle serving Okinawa-style zenzai — kintoki beans simmered for six hours under fluffy shaved ice. Its signature uses Yomitan's own beni-imo purple sweet potato, which dyes the ice violet under a brown-sugar syrup.

places.n: Hanaori Soba, Yomitan (花織そば)
places.w: Yomitan's flagship Okinawa-soba house on Prefectural Road 6, founded in 1988 by a former French-cuisine chef. The signature bowl tops medium-thin wavy noodles in pork-bone broth with soft-bone sōki and long-simmered pork belly; tebichi and liver-and-nira soba are also on the menu. It reopened after a renovation in 2026.

places.n: Ploughman's Lunch Bakery, Kitanakagusuku (PLOUGHMANS LUNCH BAKERY)
places.w: Bakery café in a renovated former foreign-residents' house on a jungly hilltop in Kitanakagusuku, opened in 2006 by a former Tokyo architectural designer. Its namesake one-plate Ploughman's Lunch — a British farmer's lunch of fresh vegetables with bread baked in-house — and its sandwich plates are the draw.

places.n: Sawanoya Motobu Honten (さわのや 本部本店)
places.ad: Motobu-chō (Motobu Soba Kaidō, Prefectural Route 84), Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: One of the anchors of the 'Motobu Soba Kaidō' noodle road: noodles are hand-made the old way with wood-ash lye, giving firm, flat thick noodles with a distinctive flavour (Mapple); Stars and Stripes Okinawa features it in its guide to slurping noodles like a local.
places.nat: さわのや 本部本店

places.n: Yae Shokudō, Nago (八重食堂)
places.w: A 40-plus-year-old Nago soba shop known for topping up bowls with broth from a kettle (OCVB); voted into Okinawa Times' 2023 poll of 900 noodle fans for the best soba in the north.

places.n: Sakihama Seimen, Onna (崎濱製麺)
places.w: Reopened in Yamada in April 2024 as the rebrand of a Tomari (Naha) soba shop that ran 8 years; noodles are rested 3+ days and ordered kufa (hard), regular or yafa (soft), in a clear pork-bonito-kelp shio broth with no pork bones (OTV okitive). OCVB's soba-lovers' picks feature it.

places.n: Okinawa Daiichi Hotel breakfast (沖縄第一ホテル 薬膳朝食)
places.w: A five-room hotel founded in 1955 whose medicinal-herb breakfast, devised by founder Shimabukuro Yoshiko from her mother's recipes about 40 years ago, uses some 50 ingredients across 20+ Okinawan dishes (about ¥3,300). One of Naha's famous breakfasts; reservation advised.
places.nat: 沖縄第一ホテル 薬膳朝食

places.n: Adachiya, Makishi (足立屋)
places.ad: Market arcade beside the former Makishi Public Market, Makishi, Naha, Okinawa
places.w: Morning-opening standing kushikatsu bar in the covered arcade by the old public market — Naha's best-known senbero (three drinks and a dish for about ¥1,000), with motsu-nikomi, kushikatsu and squid rings; busy with locals and visitors alike.

places.n: Ryūkyū Shinmen Tondō, Oroku Honten (琉球新麺 通堂 小禄本店)
places.w: The flagship of Okinawa's best-known ramen brand, billed as the world's first 'ramen with a gender': a thick, smooth tonkotsu 'men's taste' and a clear salt-chicken 'women's taste'. Open straight through from 11:00 to late night and packed with locals and visitors. The brand was also selected as a guest shop at the Shin-Yokohama Rāmen Museum.
places.nat: 琉球新麺 通堂 小禄本店

places.n: BACAR OKINAWA, Kumoji (バカール オキナワ)
places.w: Neapolitan pizzeria by Nakamura Daisuke, trained at Tokyo's SAVOY/Seirinkan: wood-fired pies with charred, chewy and crisp textures in one slice, plus starters built on Okinawan produce. Dinner only, closed Tue–Wed.
places.nat: バカール オキナワ

places.n: Ōshiro Tempura, Ōjima (大城てんぷら店)
places.w: One of the three tempura stands on 'tempura island' Ōjima, under shade trees right by the water; fish, vegetable and squid tempura are fried after you order, for a few coins apiece.

places.n: Ryūkyū no Shuki to Awamori Oninoude, Tsuboya (琉球ノ酒器ト泡盛 オニノウデ)
places.w: Awamori bar opened in July 2016 by sake-vessel collector Sakukawa Nagamasa, about 10 minutes' walk from Kokusai-dōri toward the Nōren market; some 400 awamori, many from the outer islands, poured from Okinawan karakara/chibugwā flasks and works by noted potters. Named for the long 'ogre's arm' bottle of old Ryūkyū; picked in BRUTUS's Naha bar issue.
places.nat: 琉球ノ酒器ト泡盛 オニノウデ

places.n: Kinjō Bakery, Shuri (金城ベーカリー)
places.w: Neighbourhood bakery founded in 1952 by Kinjō Mutsuhide, a minute from Gibo monorail station, still baking about 50 kinds of nostalgic breads; added an 'omiso melon pan' using miso from Shuri's royal-era Tamanahauso. Eat-in space runs a one-hour bread buffet.

places.n: Sakaemachi Bottleneck (栄町ボトルネック)
places.w: Shōwa-mood sakaba in a former house down an alley at the west entrance of Sakaemachi Market, credited as one of the core shops of the 'second Sakaemachi boom' that drew a younger crowd to the post-war market; awamori, Okinawan snacks and a soba to finish.

places.n: Okinawan Restaurant Jimanya, Naha (じまんや 那覇店)
places.w: Okinawan restaurant in a renovated 50-year-old Okinawan house about five minutes from Miebashi station, cooking with Okinawa-raised pineapple pork and island vegetables; signature thick pork-loin tonteki, and an awamori master picks a label to suit you. English menu.

places.n: Daitō Soba Kokusai-dōri (大東そば 国際通り店)
places.w: Near Midorigaoka Park off Kokusai-dōri, the one place in Naha serving the Minami-Daitō Island soul food: thick curly noodles meant to evoke the island's rough seas, in a light pork broth, with Daitō-zushi. The owner spent a year recreating the original shop's recipe after it closed in 2022 and kept its logo.
places.nat: 大東そば 国際通り店

places.n: BAR Owl, Kumoji (バー オウル)
places.ad: Kanetomo Sangyō Bldg 2F, 1-8-7 Kumoji, Naha, Okinawa 〒900-0015
places.w: Cocktail bar in Naha's Kumoji business district behind a heavy door, with a counter lined with tropical fruit; known for showy seasonal-fruit cocktails such as Okinawan mikan, and awamori cocktails. Selected for Tabelog's Bar 100 (2022).

places.n: Yappari Steak 1st, Cocktail Plaza (やっぱりステーキ 1st カクテルプラザ店)
places.w: The founding store of the Okinawa-born steak chain: it opened in Matsuyama in February 2015 as a six-seat counter selling a ¥1,000 steak, drew queues by word of mouth and grew into a nationwide chain of some 90 shops within eight years (profiled on TV Tokyo's Cambria Palace). Continues Okinawa's post-war steak-dinner culture.
places.nat: やっぱりステーキ 1st カクテルプラザ店

places.n: Señor Taco, Plaza House (セニョール ターコ)
places.ad: Plaza House 1F, 3-1-6 Kubota, Okinawa City, Okinawa 904-0023, Japan
places.w: Opened in 1984 inside Plaza House, Señor Taco is a pioneer of Okinawa's taco scene whose shells are fried crisp outside and chewy inside; it has been loved for more than 30 years and also serves Mexican dishes like enchiladas and onion rings.
places.nat: セニョール ターコ

places.n: Cafe Ocean, Gate 2 Street (カフェ オーシャン)
places.w: Founded in 1967, Ocean is the oldest taco shop on Koza's Gate 2 Street in front of Kadena Air Base, frying hand-made tortillas to order with a home-style sauce taught by Americans. A taco-and-music café-bar from the post-war 'A-sign' era.
places.nat: カフェ オーシャン

places.n: Suba-dokoro Wachichi, Okinawa City (すば処 うゎちち)
places.w: An Okinawa-soba specialist in Hiyagon whose seared soft-bone soba was certified as an Okinawa City 'Koza Choice' brand; the clear pork-and-bonito broth comes with a choice of noodles from two well-known local noodle makers. It placed 12th in OTV Okitive's reader soba ranking TOP30.

places.n: Daruma Soba, Okinawa City (だるまそば)
places.w: A hearty, queue-drawing soba shop with a pork-bone and bonito broth, chewy noodles and an unusually long menu; listed 4th in KozaWeb's Okinawa City soba ranking and 19th in OTV Okitive's reader soba TOP30.

places.n: Banjutei, Yomitan (番所亭)
places.w: A long-loved Yomitan soba house named after the old Kina banjo (district office), known for its house-made noodles, including turmeric-kneaded soba and yomogi or purple-sweet-potato variations.

places.n: Player's Cafe, Koza (プレイヤーズカフェ)
places.ad: 2-6-47 Chūō (Park Avenue), Okinawa City, Okinawa 904-0004, Japan
places.w: Opened in 1999 on Koza's Park Avenue, this café hosts live music of all genres and doubles as the lounge of Tripshot Hotels Koza; its menu draws on the owner's memories of 1970s Koza home cooking shaped by US-military canned goods. Ryukyu Shimpo reported its lunch sets as a hit with a wide range of customers.

places.n: Cafe Hakoniwa, Motobu (Cafe ハコニワ)
places.ad: 2566 Izumi, Motobu-chō, Kunigami District, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: A 50-plus-year-old house in the Izumi hills, turned into a café with antique furniture. The signature is the Hakoniwa plate, home-style rice and side dishes made with locally grown vegetables. There are also cakes and shīkwāsā juice. Closed Wednesdays and Thursdays.

places.n: Cafe Kokuu, Nakijin (カフェこくう)
places.ad: 2031-138 Moroshi, Nakijin-son, Kunigami District, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: A hilltop café in Nakijin whose cooking draws on Japanese and macrobiotic food. The signature Kokuu plate serves more than ten kinds of organically grown island vegetables, each cooked a different way, on yachimun pottery. Closed Sundays and Mondays.

places.n: Iejima Distillery, Ie Island (伊江島蒸留所)
places.ad: 1627-3 Higashi-Ebusaki, Ie-son, Kunigami District, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: The island's rum distillery, set up in a former bioethanol demonstration plant, makes Ie Rum Santa Maria as agricole rum from local sugarcane juice. It won Best Japanese Rum of the Year at the first Tokyo Whiskey & Spirits Competition in 2019. A distillery-limited bottling took a top gold medal in the 2026 edition. The island is a 30-minute ferry ride from Motobu Port.

places.n: Tōfu no Higa, Ishigaki (とうふの比嘉)
places.w: A family tofu maker of more than 70 years, now run by the third generation, that opens at 6:30 am and sells out before noon. It is known for yushi-dōfu, tofu ladled out before it sets. The Kariyushi set adds egg, rice or porridge, okara and soy milk. Closed Sundays.

places.n: Okinawa Soba Marukami, Miyako (沖縄そば まるかみ)
places.ad: 91 Kurima (下地来間), Shimoji, Kurima Island, Miyakojima-shi, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: A soba shop in the Kurima settlement on Kurima Island, run by a former hotel-restaurant cook. The house Marukami soba comes with homemade fresh noodles and bonito broth, topped with seasoned pork belly, tender cartilage sōki and a thin egg crepe. A plain su-soba is also on the menu. Lunch only, 11:00–14:30.
places.nat: 沖縄そば まるかみ

places.n: Zhyvago Coffee Works Okinawa, Chatan (ジバゴコーヒーワークス)
places.ad: Distortion Seaside Bldg, 9-46 Mihama, Chatan-chō, Nakagami District, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: A West Coast-style coffee stand on the Mihama seafront, opened in 2015, that makes each cup to order. The Ryukyu Shimpo profiled Kotaro Mikami, the Chatan Zhyvago shop manager, as the Japan AeroPress Championship winner. The brand also co-developed a coffee with JTA airline to go with chinsukō.
places.nat: ジバゴコーヒーワークス

places.n: Jikasei-men Okinawa Soba Miyoya, Kadena (自家製麺 沖縄そば みよ家)
places.w: An Okinawa-soba specialist in Kadena making its own noodles and an additive-free broth from Rausu kombu and Makurazaki bonito; its curry soba is a signature. OTV Okitive ranked it No. 3 in its 2025 island-wide 'must-eat' Okinawa soba 15.
places.nat: 自家製麺 沖縄そば みよ家

places.n: TESIO, Koza Gate Street (テシオ)
places.w: A ham-and-sausage maker on Koza's Gate Street, opened April 2017 by an Okinawan trained in German charcuterie methods; its products have won gold medals at IFFA, the German international meat-processing competition. Sausages are made by hand daily and a weekend hot-dog counter serves them in-shop.

places.n: Yaezen, Motobu (八重善)
places.w: A soba stop on Motobu's Route 84 'soba road', named by the OCVB soba-road itinerary for its signature bowl that combines Okinawa soba with squid-ink broth made with fresh local white squid. rurubu lists the ikasumi soba as limited to 10 servings a day, plus sōki soba and the seasonal 'Yaezen gozen' set.

places.n: Nakijin Soba (今帰仁そば)
places.w: An Okinawa soba shop in an old Ryūkyū house in a fukugi-lined village near Churaumi, known for its light but rich broth and melting nankotsu sōki. When it faced closure, fans of the shop took it over; it reopened renewed in its 10th year with outdoor seating (Okinawa Times), and ran a limited Naha pop-up in 2026.

places.n: Famille tacos, Nago (Famille)
places.w: A takeout taco stand opened in July 2025 on the national road to Junglia by a couple who cooked in French hotel restaurants; the meat takes three days to develop its flavour. Covered by Okinawa Times and Ryukyu Shimpo, and ranked No. 2 in the north in OTV Okitive's 2026 Golden Week 30, which says its 200 tacos a day sell out.

places.n: Ryūkyū Ryōri Nago-magari Restaurant, Nago (名護曲レストラン)
places.w: A long-running Ryukyu-cuisine restaurant on the coast road at Yofuke in Nago, listed by rurubu, Okinawa Traveler and the OCVB; rurubu notes the owner builds menus from rare and nutritious seasonal ingredients. The wide menu runs from Okinawan set meals and soba to Western dishes like taco rice and steak.

places.n: CAFE FUKURUBI, Kouri Island (カフェ フクルビ)
places.w: A café-restaurant on high ground near Heart Rock on Kouri Island's north side, with a 180-degree panorama of the horizon from its terrace. It cooks with prefectural ingredients and especially Kouri Island's own pure brown sugar, used in its signature black-sugar French toast.

places.n: Kōhī Sakan Inshallah, Kokusai-dōri (珈琲茶館インシャラー)
places.w: Coffee house on Kokusai-dōri trading since 1974, themed on Arabia as coffee's birthplace and serving Turkish and Arabic coffees. Its signature 'Paris no Romance' has rose cream swirling in the cup as the coffee is poured at the table.
places.nat: 珈琲茶館インシャラー

places.n: Live House Shimauta, Kokusai-dōri (ライブハウス島唄)
places.ad: Haisai Okinawa Bldg 3F, 1-2-31 Makishi, Naha, Okinawa
places.w: Home stage of Nēnēs, the women's vocal group credited with sparking the shima-uta boom; they play several nights a week (three sets a night), with other local acts on the rest. Okinawan food and drink served, no time limit on the live charge.

places.n: Okinawa Soba Kintarō, Nanjō (沖縄そば 金太郎)
places.w: A local soba shop in Tamagusuku-Funakoshi known for a rich pork-bone soup and huge 'Jirō-inspired' bowls heaped with vegetables, with a three-meat Okinawa soba as its standard. Its owner chairs the Nanjō Okinawa-soba stamp rally promoting the city as a soba town.

places.n: Yukui-dokoro Washima, Kume Island (ゆくい処 笑島)
places.w: Kume-jima's kuruma-prawn soba, built on an Okinawa-soba dashi with a paste of the island's farmed kuruma prawns and local miso, won the grand prix at the 'Nippon no Takaramono' world competition held in Singapore. The shop sells around 60 bowls a day and often sells out.

places.n: Wayama Mozuku, Zamami (和山海雲)
places.w: A mozuku farmer's own restaurant three minutes' walk from Zamami port, serving soba made with thick mozuku grown in the Kerama sea; Okinawa Times praised the firm noodles' match with the seaweed's texture. It also sells its mozuku and runs snorkel tours.

places.n: Boku no Mise Ojisan, Zamami (ぼくの店 おじさん)
places.w: A local favourite three minutes' walk from Zamami port, known for a hearty katsudon alongside soba and chanpurū lunch plates. It is listed on Zamami Village's official guide map.
places.nat: ぼくの店 おじさん

places.n: Minatomachi Parlor, Itoman (港町パーラー)
places.ad: 989-83 Itoman, Itoman, Okinawa, Japan (Itoman Market Itomāru)
places.w: A small counter opened in April 2025 inside Itoman's public market 'Itomāru' by the second-generation head of Kinshiro Sengyo, a fish shop trading in Itoman for 35+ years; the owner fillets the day's catch on the spot for generous local-fish bowls. Ryukyu Shimpo's 'Uchinā Ajimāi' series and OTV Okitive both featured it.

places.n: Kikunotsuyu Shuzō awamori distillery, Miyako (菊之露酒造)
places.w: Founded in 1928 in Hirara, Kikunotsuyu is one of Miyako's oldest and best-known awamori distillers, using the island's mineral-rich hard water from its coral-limestone bedrock; its aged awamori features in the Okinawa Regional Taxation Bureau's awamori appraisal.

places.n: Ikemajima gelato cafe Ninufa, Ikema Island (ニヌファ)
places.w: An Italian-style gelato café on Ikema Island whose name means 'North Star' in Miyako dialect; every seat on its coral-rock terrace faces the sea. Gelato is made without artificial flavouring, colouring or preservatives in local flavours, with wood-fired pizza alongside.

places.n: Ishigaki City Public Market (石垣市公設市場)
places.w: Ishigaki's 'kitchen' since 1899 (on this site since 1904), a three-storey public market in the Euglena Mall arcade: local produce and fish at street level, the Ishigaki City specialty-products centre above and a shokudō on top; an eat-in space was added in the May 2021 renewal.

places.n: Okinohikari Shuzō awamori distillery, Miyako (沖之光酒造)
places.w: Founded in 1948 (as Kosa Shuzō; Okinohikari since 1979), this Hirara distillery keeps about 70 % of its stock as aged kūsu; its 100 % ten-year-aged Okinohikari won the Okinawa Regional Taxation Bureau Director's Award at the 2005 awamori appraisal.

places.n: Yuunami Sakashita (自家製生麺 ゆうなみ 坂下店)
places.ad: Terrace Sakashita 1F, 301-15 Matsukawa, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: A local Okinawa-soba shop whose house-made fresh noodles are blended with whole-wheat flour. You can pick thin, flat or mugwort noodles for the signature nankotsu sōki soba, and the pork-and-bonito broth is rich enough to drink to the last drop. Readers voted it into the Okinawa Times 2023 '900 noodle lovers pick' Okinawa-soba ranking (southern edition).
places.nat: 自家製生麺 ゆうなみ 坂下店

places.n: Soba-dokoro Kikuya, Oroku (そば処 きくや)
places.w: A red-tiled house next to the owner's home, about five minutes by car from Naha Airport. The light broth of pork bone, bonito, kombu and vegetables is simmered for two days. The menu has sanmai-niku soba, yushi-tōfu soba and black-sugar zenzai, and it closes when sold out (around 3 pm). It was picked in the Okinawa Times 2023 reader poll of Okinawa-soba shops (southern edition).

places.n: Okinawa Jiryōri Angama, Kokusai-dōri (沖縄地料理 あんがま)
places.w: An Okinawan-cuisine and folk-song restaurant just inside the south entrance of Kokusai-dōri. The entrance is built like a red-tiled, stone-walled house and is topped by a giant mask from Ishigaki's Angama Bon festival. The menu has about 60 dishes made with island vegetables, pork and local seafood, including gōyā chanpurū, tebichi and sōki-ni, plus four set courses. Min'yō singers play every night in the third-floor hall.
places.nat: 沖縄地料理 あんがま

places.n: Shima-uta to Jiryōri Tubarama, Kokusai-dōri (島唄と地料理 とぅばらーま)
places.w: An Okinawan-cuisine restaurant on Kokusai-dōri, a one-minute walk from Makishi Station, with an interior that recreates a pre-war Okinawan townscape. Lunch is Okinawa soba and chanpurū set meals, and sanshin shima-uta (island-song) bands play every night. OTV Okitive featured it for blending tradition with modern twists such as an Okinawan-style fried rice.
places.nat: 島唄と地料理 とぅばらーま

places.n: Chiikawa Restaurant Okinawa, PARCO CITY Urasoe (ちいかわレストラン 沖縄店)
places.ad: San-A Urasoe Nishi-Kaigan PARCO CITY, 3-1-1 Irijima, Urasoe, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: The second permanent Chiikawa Restaurant in Japan after Ikebukuro PARCO, a family-restaurant-style character café that opened on 13 February 2026 inside San-A Urasoe Nishi-Kaigan PARCO CITY. Alongside the shared grand menu it serves Okinawa-only dishes: the 'sunburnt shīsā' taco rice, a 'mensōre' banana split and a shīsā sanpin-tea tropical drink.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Chiikawa (ちいかわ, Nagano's manga/anime) — only the 2nd permanent Chiikawa Restaurant nationwide, with Okinawa-exclusive menu
places.nat: ちいかわレストラン 沖縄店

places.n: Taishū Shokudō Mickey, Park Avenue (大衆食堂ミッキー)
places.w: A decades-old one-woman shokudō on Koza's Park Avenue carrying on her mother's recipes; OTV Okitive profiled its never-shared 'secret' family flavour, and KozaWeb lists it among Koza's taco-rice and A-sign-era diners. The okazu plate of five vegetables and island tofu is the house signature.

places.n: Sam's Anchor Inn Ginowan (サムズアンカーイン 宜野湾店)
places.w: The founding branch of Okinawa's Sam's steak chain, opened on Route 58 in Mashiki in August 1970 by American Ray Payne; its then-novel teppanyaki show and original menu of shrimp cocktail and tenderloin made it a pre-reversion steak institution. The Ryukyu Shimpo marked the chain's 55th anniversary in 2025.
places.nat: サムズアンカーイン 宜野湾店

places.n: Maeda Soba, Enobi (前田そば)
places.w: A small soba shop near the Enobi crossroads that the Ryukyu Shimpo's gourmet column praised for a simple, deeply flavoured bowl drawing soba fans from across the island; OTV Okitive featured its limited-quantity bone-broth soba made with Kin-Agu pork. Closes when sold out.

places.n: Subaya Yūbaru Menkata, Uruma (すば家 ゆーばる麺方)
places.w: A family soba house opened in July 2025 by the min'yō singer Kamiya Chihiro's family under their Tsuken-jima house name, carrying on the 'Yūbaru soba' served at the family's Tsuken Island minshuku. The Okinawa Times and OTV Okitive both featured its local-produce set meals with sanmai-niku and Shirikawa tofu.
places.nat: すば家 ゆーばる麺方

places.n: Ippe Coppe, Minatogawa Stateside Town (ippe coppe いっぺこっぺ)
places.w: A natural-yeast bakery in a converted 1950s–60s American military house in Urasoe's Minatogawa Stateside Town, specialising in additive-free shokupan made from Hokkaido 'Harutaka' flour; Tabirai and Mapple both single it out and Urasoe's own tourism site lists it. Opens 12:30 and closes when sold out.
places.nat: ippe coppe いっぺこっぺ

places.n: Sakaemachi Kai Senmon Sakaba Hiikiya (栄町貝専門酒場 ひいき屋)
places.w: A red-lantern counter bar in Sakaemachi Market that serves only shellfish. It usually has 25 or more kinds of seasonal shellfish from around Japan and Okinawa, rising past 35 at peak season. The counter faces the market lane, and Tabirai describes it as a place where you easily get talking to locals ('ichariba chōdē').
places.nat: 栄町貝専門酒場 ひいき屋

places.n: Okinawa Soba Senmonten Charu Soba, Sakaemachi (沖縄そば専門店 ちゃるそば)
places.w: An Okinawa-soba specialist inside Sakaemachi Market. Okinawa Times called its cloudy, bonito-scented broth 'one of a kind'. Soft-bone sōki and pork-belly soba come with jūshī rice, and the evening menu adds a senbero drinks set.
places.nat: 沖縄そば専門店 ちゃるそば

places.n: Teshiraji Soba, Shuri (てぃしらじそば 汀志良次)
places.w: A small soba shop on Route 82, about halfway between Shuri and Gibo monorail stations. It takes its name from the old village of Tishiraji. The owner, who quit an office job to open it, makes and hand-rubs the curly noodles from the day before and serves them in a very clear broth topped with needle ginger rather than red pickled ginger. It closes when the soba sells out.
places.nat: てぃしらじそば 汀志良次

places.n: Marutaka Soba, Nago (丸隆そば)
places.w: A Nago soba house founded in 1948 (formerly Ganaha Soba) that OTV Okitive presents as a 70-plus-year institution serving the 'original' sōki soba — flat wide noodles in a bonito-forward broth. Listed by the Nago City tourism association.

places.n: Hammock Garden Anettai Chaya, Motobu (亜熱帯茶屋)
places.w: An Asian-style hillside café opened in May 2015 up a single-lane lane in Motobu, near Churaumi, with hammocks, arbours and mostly outdoor seats looking over forest and sea. Stars and Stripes Okinawa reviewed it for its food and coastal view; the OCVB, Mapple and Tabirai list its brunch toasts and Yanbaru-herb chicken gapao rice.

places.n: CASA SOL, Nakijin (カーサソル)
places.w: A forest-hill café over the Haneji inland sea opened on 17 September 2024 by a YouTuber couple, built from glass-walled containers with a driftwood 'bird's nest' lookout and a giant swing (OTV Okitive, Tabirai). Its menu draws on the owners' world travels — açai bowls made without frozen fruit, poke bowls, smoothies and morning plates; rurubu ranks it among Okinawa's six best Yanbaru forest cafés.

places.n: Taco Rice Café Kijimunā, Senaga-jima Umikaji Terrace (タコライスcafe きじむなぁ 瀬長島ウミカジテラス店)
places.w: The Umikaji Terrace branch of Kijimunā, the shop that created 'omu-taco' (taco rice under a soft omelette) in Onna in 2003 and has since won awards at Okinawa gourmet festivals. Rurubu picks it among Umikaji Terrace's recommended eats and Okinawa Traveler includes it in its seven popular taco-rice shops.
places.nat: タコライスcafe きじむなぁ 瀬長島ウミカジテラス店

places.n: Restaurant Namiji, Kume Island (レストラン波路)
places.ad: 548-32 Janadō, Kumejima, Shimajiri District, Okinawa, Japan
places.w: An island restaurant in Janadō that the Okinawa Times profiles for its spread of local seafood — Kume-jima's farmed kuruma-ebi prawns, mozuku seaweed, and ikasumi-jiru squid-ink soup — drawing both tourists and residents. The Kume-jima Tourism Association lists it among the island's eateries and notes the soups can be added to a lunch set cheaply.

places.n: Hawaiian Pancake Cafe KOA, Itoman (Hawaiian Pancake Cafe KOA)
places.ad: Itoman, Okinawa, Japan (beachfront; Stars and Stripes GPS N26.117810 E127.662568 — street number not captured)
places.w: A beachfront Hawaiian café in Itoman that the Ryukyu Shimpo's 'Uchinā Ajimāi' column (no. 144) calls stylish and generous. Stars and Stripes Okinawa recommends its hearty loco moco and pancakes, with an ocean view, as a refuel stop on a southern-Okinawa drive.

places.n: Oyaji no Maguro, Senaga-jima Umikaji Terrace (親父のまぐろ)
places.ad: Senaga-jima Umikaji Terrace, 174-6 Senaga, Tomigusuku, Okinawa 901-0233, Japan
places.w: A tuna-bowl counter at Umikaji Terrace where a fisherman father line-catches the tuna and his son and daughter-in-law serve it fresh and never frozen. It is known for thick-cut yellowfin maguro-don and an ahi poke rice. Rurubu lists it among the terrace's recommended eats and the Ryukyu Shimpo has profiled it.

places.n: Koshibaru Shokudō, Miyako (腰原食堂)
places.w: A Hirara soba shokudō whose house creation is the spicy 'dragon soba', made by adding Chinese-style chicken stock to the bonito-and-pork Miyako soba broth; it also serves a plain Miyako soba. Mapple lists it among Miyako's ten most popular Miyako soba lunch spots.

places.n: Cafe Uesuya, Miyako (カフェ ウエスヤ)
places.w: A creative Asian café opened in 2014 on a Hirara back lane (in the owner's grandfather's former dental clinic) and since relocated within Shimozato, Hirara. At lunch it serves three original takes on Miyako soba; the signature 'Asian Miyako soba' is a pho-like bowl topped with coriander, nira and tomato.

places.n: Shima Soba Ichiban-chi Ishigaki Honten (島そば一番地 石垣本店)
places.w: A Yaeyama-soba specialist named for its address, 'Aza-Ishigaki No. 1', a short walk from Ishigaki port's remote-island terminal (it also has a Naha branch). Tabirai's list of ten must-eat Yaeyama soba shops on Ishigaki includes it, and Rurubu features it.
places.nat: 島そば一番地 石垣本店

places.n: Café Tēdun Shidamē-kan, Taketomi Island (カフェ てぇーどぅん しだめー館)
places.w: A red-tiled café beneath the Nagomi-no-tō lookout in Taketomi village, about 12 minutes' walk from the port. It was one of the winners at the first Yaeyama Soba Championship in 2015, the year Komatsu took the Yaeyama-soba grand prix.
places.nat: カフェ てぇーどぅん しだめー館

places.n: Ikehara Shuzō awamori distillery, Ishigaki (池原酒造)
places.w: A family awamori distillery in central Ishigaki, founded in 1951, that makes a single brand, Shirayuri ('white lily'). Tabirai profiles it in its series on Okinawa's awamori distilleries.
